cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Convert one rotation to radians and the period to seconds.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Using minutes in a rate expressed per second

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Compare the radial force balances at the top and bottom and check the other consequences of constant speed.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Treating tension as the whole centripetal force

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Distinguish a negative potential from its magnitude and compare the inverse-square field across a fixed separation.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming a fixed separation implies a fixed field-strength difference

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Account for the momentum reversal, then use collision rate and Newton’s third law.

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Set up a heat balance using the unequal masses and specific heat capacities.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Averaging the temperatures without weighting by heat capacity

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Identify the melting plateau and convert its duration into energy per kilogram.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Reading temperature change as absolute temperature

cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student checks the initial energy and counts the equilibrium crossings.
cjc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Giving potential energy the same period as displacement

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Single application of the rule for combining percentage uncertainties with a power.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to multiply the uncertainty of a squared quantity by its power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Needs vector subtraction for relative velocity, a common slip in direction.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Adding velocities instead of subtracting, or finding Q relative to P

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires treating the hole as negative mass and taking a weighted average of centres.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Ignoring the removed area or measuring the hole position from the wrong edge

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Combines F = BIL with N turns and a principle-of-moments calculation using the correct perpendicular distances.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Using the wrong perpendicular distances or forgetting that only the bottom side is in the field

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Direct link between constant force, constant acceleration and a linear velocity rise.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Thinking velocity follows the force, or that the body stops when the force is removed

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: One application of F = ma with resistive force included.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Forgetting the resistive force or using only ma

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Two-step: useful power from P = Fv, then input power from energy per minute.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Forgetting to convert energy per minute into power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires recognising the ball still has horizontal KE at the top and estimating its fraction.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking KE is zero at the top of the trajectory

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Direct use of relative speed of approach equals relative speed of separation.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming the masses are equal, or that P must stop or keep going forward

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Straight substitution into a = rω² with ω = 2π/T and a unit conversion.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Forgetting the cm to m conversion or omitting 2π

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires knowing field lines are perpendicular to equipotentials and point to lower potential.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Thinking the field points towards higher (less negative) potential

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Uses φ ∝ 1/r and the fact that the field weakens with distance.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking potential difference stays the same for a fixed separation, as in a uniform field

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs phase reasoning from a to x to v and recognising KE has half the period.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Forgetting that kinetic energy oscillates at twice the frequency of displacement

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Needs timing of travel to and from the fixed end plus the phase inversion on reflection.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Forgetting that a pulse reflected at a fixed end is inverted, or reversing the order of its parts

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Combines intensity proportional to source power and inverse-square distance.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Applying only one of the two changes, or using 1/r instead of 1/r²

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs to halve the 60° angle before using d sinθ = nλ and to convert to lines per mm.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the full angle between orders instead of the angle from the normal

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs the Rayleigh criterion with an estimated visible wavelength.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using a wrong wavelength order of magnitude for visible light

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Uses ΔU as a state function across two paths with careful sign convention.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Thinking heat transfer is the same for both paths, or mixing up sign conventions

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Simple heat balance where c cancels and mass is proportional to volume.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Swapping which mass goes with which temperature

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires scaling E with Q/r² and combining field directions correctly.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Subtracting the fields because the charges have opposite signs

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Single application of $I = nAvq$ with two ratio changes.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Forgetting that area scales with diameter squared

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Potential divider reasoning with standard NTC and LDR behaviour.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking resistance of an NTC thermistor rises with temperature

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Needs to identify series/parallel arrangement then combine capacitances and use $Q = CV$.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Treating all capacitors as in parallel, or charge as the sum on each capacitor

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Combines r.m.s.-to-peak conversion with the $\sin^2$ shape of power.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using the r.m.s. current as the peak, or a $|\sin|$ shape for power

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires 3D direction reasoning for both forces on a negative charge across four field combinations.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming E and B must always be perpendicular for undeflected motion

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct use of flux cut $= BLvt$ with unit conversions.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Forgetting to convert minutes to seconds or cm to m

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Linking intensity to photon energy or wave amplitude

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires understanding which position and momentum components the slit constrains.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Taking $\Delta p$ along the direction of travel or $\Delta y$ at the screen

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Applies $\beta^-$ decay changes to a nuclide chart.
cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Swapping proton and neutron changes in beta decay

cjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the Rutherford scattering interpretation.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student needs everyday estimates in SI units.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student converts the spring constant to base units and matches two exponents.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Reversing the time exponent of the spring constant

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student recognises the subtraction construction using a common tip.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Adding the vectors when asked to subtract

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student resolves the weight along the slope and applies constant-acceleration kinematics.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Using free-fall acceleration along the slope

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student resolves the initial velocity and uses zero vertical velocity at the apex.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Omitting the square of the initial vertical speed

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student distinguishes the sign of the gradient from its magnitude.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming increasing force magnitude requires increasing momentum

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student matches the forces by both the bodies and the interaction.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Pairing balanced forces acting on the same body

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student computes the displaced volume and balances the upthrust against weight.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Using the full pipe length as the submerged depth

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student infers the extension from a graph of length against tension.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Using total length as the extension

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student recognises the equations connecting work and the change in speed.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Using final speed as a constant speed during acceleration

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student identifies both useful outputs and reconstructs the total input power.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Counting only electrical output as useful

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student identifies the limiting point and sets the tension there to zero.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Overlooking the zero-tension condition at the top

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student determines the reachable surface and converts the potential drop into kinetic energy per unit mass.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Using an absolute potential instead of a potential difference

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student derives the orbital kinetic energy and compares how all three energies vary with radius.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming total energy is conserved when the orbit is raised

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must compare work across two thermodynamic paths at the same volumes.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming a return to the original volume restores internal energy.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must equate heat-loss rates across cooling and solidification.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Ignoring the cooling rate when comparing the heat transfers.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must extract a temperature ratio from the isotherms and then take its square root.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Treating r.m.s. speed as proportional to temperature.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must identify how much charge passes a fixed point per revolution.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Using tangential speed as the charge passage frequency.

dhs-2021-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish total energy supplied from energy dissipated internally and apply two electrical energy relations.
dhs-2021-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Using total source energy to calculate the internal resistance.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The conversion uses one familiar prefix and one change to scientific notation.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating giga as a smaller power of ten.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must compare the readings both with each other and with the true value.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing repeatability with closeness to the true value.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must recognize equivalent forms of the uniform-acceleration equations.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using half the change in velocity as the average velocity.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must read velocity from the graph’s gradient and recognize terminal motion.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Drawing a horizontal displacement–time line for terminal velocity.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a gravitational third-law pair from the forces balancing on the book.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Pairing the book’s weight with its normal force.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must track energy during contact as well as before and after the bounce.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming an elastic collision keeps kinetic energy constant throughout contact.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must find both lever arms from the rear wheel before balancing moments.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the interval between the forces as both lever arms.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must link pressure to contact force and express mass in terms of density and volume.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Retaining cross-sectional area after it cancels.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must find both mechanical-energy changes and take their difference.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Equating all lost gravitational potential energy with frictional dissipation.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must convert the pumping time to seconds and use efficiency to recover the pump input power.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing useful pump output with useful engine output.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The shared angular speed cancels in a direct centripetal-force ratio.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming the masses share a linear speed.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The inverse-square law must be combined with how mass scales at fixed density.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Holding mass fixed when the sphere grows.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation requires the orbital radius and the period implied by geostationary motion.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using altitude as the orbital radius.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify a half-cycle phase difference and match it to SHM variables.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing a quarter-cycle phase shift with a half-cycle shift.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must combine the squared amplitude dependence with the inverse-square period dependence.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Scaling energy linearly with amplitude or period.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student converts frequency to period and reads the horizontal length of one cycle.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the whole display width for one period.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must translate a collinear arrangement into a path difference and test for a whole number of wavelengths.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using one source-to-observer distance as the path difference.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish changes to the central maximum width from changes to the total transmitted light.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming a wider slit transmits the same amount of light.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must combine constant horizontal velocity and uniform vertical acceleration to obtain a square law.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Treating deflection as proportional to horizontal travel.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The ladder requires alternating voltage and current calculations across two successive junctions.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the end-branch current for all the resistors.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The familiar filament-lamp characteristic must be interpreted with voltage on the vertical axis.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Keeping the usual current-on-vertical-axis curve after swapping axes.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The equal branch voltages make the current ratio the inverse of the resistance ratio.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assigning the largest current to the largest resistance.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the angle between the current and the field is read in three dimensions.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using the field’s angle to the horizontal as its angle to the current.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The right-hand grip rule identifies the region in which the two fields can cancel.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming parallel currents produce fields in the same direction everywhere.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must trace both half-cycles and compare the total series resistance in each direction.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating opposite diodes as a full-wave rectifier or as equal-resistance paths.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must match the slopes of five flux segments to the emf graph.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using magnetic flux instead of its rate of change

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Students must account for the fixed work function when the photon energy doubles.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Scaling stopping voltage directly with photon energy

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students must identify both the location of the position constraint and the matching momentum component.
dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Pairing position and momentum uncertainties along different axes

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Students subtract proton number from mass number and check both counts against the supplied list.

dhs-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Students must estimate the background from noisy data and halve the corrected count rate.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Students compare the spread and central value of each set of repeated readings.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must substitute extreme input values into a reciprocal relationship.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students must use two constant-acceleration equations with zero initial speed.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Using final speed as the average speed

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Students must use the relative speed relation and account for X rebounding.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Equating individual speeds in an elastic collision

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must combine a triangular area with a trapezoidal area and convert centimetres to metres.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Using force times extension for a varying force

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students must balance weight against buoyancy and convert the air density to consistent units.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Using weight in place of mass after cancelling gravity

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students identify the quantity conserved during vertical motion under gravity alone.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming momentum is conserved under gravity

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students must relate the tension differences in three rod segments to the individual centripetal forces.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Using the same orbital radius for all three masses

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Students must derive the orbital period scaling and apply it to a radius ratio.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Students read the intercept and gradient directly from the Celsius-to-kelvin conversion.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Treating a temperature offset as a scale factor

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must conserve the total gas amount while tracking two different bulb temperatures.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Using a single temperature for both bulbs.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation separates the energy used to warm the liquid from the energy used to vaporise it.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Treating all heater energy as latent heat.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must read the gradient and use the downward-positive convention.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Reading the sign of the graph slope as the physical direction without checking the diagram.

dhs-2022-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must connect equilibrium with zero restoring force and maximum speed.
dhs-2022-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Expecting the restoring force to be greatest where the pendulum moves fastest.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the SI prefixes are converted.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q1.misconception: Reversing the conversion from joules to a prefixed unit.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a vector change in velocity from a change in speed.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q2.misconception: Subtracting speed magnitudes to find a velocity change.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must write force equations for both masses and eliminate the common tension.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q5.misconception: Using one hanging weight as the driving force.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The calculation requires finding the centre of each section and converting lengths into volumes.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q6.misconception: Measuring a moment arm to the end of a section.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must identify the useful energy change from the two speeds.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q8.misconception: Equating the work of the driving force with useful work regardless of losses.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must combine force balance at top speed with the power relation before taking a cube root.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q9.misconception: Applying the drag–speed law directly to power.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must combine the contact condition at the top with conservation of mechanical energy.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming the bead is stationary at the threshold of contact.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must use the orbital period in seconds and then relate angular velocity to speed.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q11.misconception: Using Earth’s daily rotation period as its orbital period.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must read four temperature changes and compare two energy balances.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming the water transfers the same amount of heat in both experiments.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The question asks for the definition of internal energy.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing internal energy with heat supplied.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must read the amplitude, square its ratio, and subtract the remaining energy fraction from one.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming oscillator energy is proportional to amplitude.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Fixed-end conditions determine the harmonic and node count.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: One inverse relationship connects frequency to the wavelength-to-width ratio.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The two point-charge formulas share a factor that cancels.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must connect width to cross-sectional area and track the common current.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q21.misconception: Assuming different currents through the two sections

dhs-2023-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The calculation links equivalent resistance, common voltage and branch current.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q22.misconception: Confusing total current with branch current

dhs-2023-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Tracing the current through the main loop and branches identifies the brightest bulb.

dhs-2023-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The photon momentum formula immediately identifies its dependence on wavelength.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing photon flux with momentum per photon

dhs-2023-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must balance the reaction, convert bulk energy to energy per reaction and compare binding energies.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing binding energy with released energy

dhs-2023-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The remaining parent fraction must be compared with the fraction that decayed.
dhs-2023-other-p1-q30.misconception: Using initial parent count for daughter count

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must subtract velocities as vectors and identify the canceling horizontal components.

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must compare the cars’ signed velocities before and after the graphs cross.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Equating closest approach with one car stopping

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must identify which conservation law depends on the collision being elastic.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Assuming steel-bob collisions must be elastic

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the interface depth is identified.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using depth of the tube opening

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must combine the zero-normal-force condition with energy conservation.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Setting speed to zero at the contact threshold

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must combine opposing field vectors and same-sign scalar potentials.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Treating gravitational potential as a vector

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Students convert the molar mass and temperature before substituting into the ideal gas equation.

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Students find the new angle and convert the intensity ratio to an amplitude ratio.

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Students relate the halved area to resistance per unit length and recognise that the current stays the same.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Assuming current changes at a constriction

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Students apply Fleming’s left-hand rule to a tilted field and a current into the page.

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students track how the rod cuts field lines during three stages of motion.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using total speed instead of motion across the field

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students compare the two mean powers and distinguish the new peak current from its r.m.s. value.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Reporting peak current as r.m.s. current

dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students recognise the physical origin of position–momentum uncertainty.
dhs-2023-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Attributing quantum uncertainty to instrument resolution

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students subtract velocity vectors using the unchanged horizontal component.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students account for the changes in both distance and acceleration before taking a square root.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Scaling time instead of time squared

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Students compare both signed velocities to determine when the separation changes from decreasing to increasing.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Using one car’s zero velocity as the turning point for separation

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Students find the common acceleration and choose a different subsystem for each contact force.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Treating contact force as the net force on one block

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students combine perpendicular tensions and use the cord slopes to assign the larger tension.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Ignoring the horizontal balance of the two tensions

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students apply the displaced-water rule when submerged and force balance when floating.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Taking the reciprocal of the requested upthrust ratio

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students combine force balance with the power relation to obtain a cubic speed dependence.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Treating drag as proportional to engine power

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students distinguish the common angular velocity from the different tangential speeds.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming all points on a rigid turntable have the same linear speed

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing apparent weight from gravitational force.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must compare how orbital quantities depend on radius.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Treating orbital angular speed as independent of radius.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: It requires setting the starting phase and converting displacement into a scale reading.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing displacement from equilibrium with position on the scale.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must infer the motion period from the energy graph and link peak energy to peak acceleration.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Taking the kinetic-energy period as the oscillation period.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: It requires relating the width to cross-sectional area and recognizing that both sections carry the same current.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming that series sections with the same current have the same voltage gradient.

dhs-2023-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: It requires checking diode bias and whether the circuit can maintain a positive fixed output voltage.
dhs-2023-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming the two resistance changes cancel in the potential divider.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: It requires a single check of SI base units.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating a dimensionally inconsistent expression as a possible speed.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: It requires subtracting vectors and identifying the correct signed direction.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: It uses standard kinematics but requires separating the reaction and braking intervals.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: It requires comparing signed velocities before and after an elastic collision.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating momentum conservation alone as sufficient for an elastic collision.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing a third-law pair from two forces that balance on one object.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Pairing two balancing forces on the same body.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: It requires matching each force to its initial value and its trend as terminal velocity is approached.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: It requires selecting the displacement component along the lifting force.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the full displacement magnitude to compute work against gravity.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: It requires calculating thrust power, sharing it between two engines and applying efficiency.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Confusing useful output power with input power.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: It requires converting one hour to seconds and dividing one revolution by the period.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using minutes in a result expressed per second.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires finding the distance from Earth's centre before applying the inverse-square law.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using orbital height as the distance from Earth's centre.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the quantities fixed by a geostationary orbit from those that depend on satellite mass.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Equal orbital speed implies equal kinetic energy.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires recognizing that thermal equilibrium fixes the mean translational kinetic energy of both gases.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming lighter molecules have lower mean kinetic energy at the same temperature.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires using the same heat input rate to relate warming to vaporisation.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Dividing by the heating rate in the wrong energy balance.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires using the sinusoidal displacement to find a partial travel time.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming travel time is proportional to distance in SHM.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires connecting the decay of free oscillations to the driven frequency response.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Greater damping produces a higher resonance peak.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting the displacements of neighbouring particles on each side of a labelled point.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing a displacement crest with a compression.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires reading the offset between matching points as a fraction of one period.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Measuring the offset between points at different stages of the cycle.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing nodal and antinodal lines and counting their orders.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Counting constructive lines when the path difference is a half-integer wavelength.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires choosing the sign of the potential change and converting millimetres to metres.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Potential increases in the direction of the electric field.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the current path length and the area perpendicular to that path.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the area of the square surface as the current cross-section.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires relating a linear change in diameter to a nonlinear increase in drift speed.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Drift speed is inversely proportional to diameter.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires using the coordinates at a given operating point to compare resistances.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Reading resistance from the local slope of an I–V graph.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires linking electric acceleration to the force balance in crossed fields.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Inverting the charge-to-mass ratio during rearrangement.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires finding the local field direction and applying the magnetic force rule to the second wire.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Applying the attraction rule for parallel currents to perpendicular wires.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires comparing RMS currents before and after half-wave rectification.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Halving the conducting time halves the RMS current.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires inferring the polarity between the rim and axle from the magnetic force on electrons.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Steady rotation cannot induce an emf.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires calculating the momentum change on reflection and turning it into a rate.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires converting the stopping potential into a maximum kinetic energy before subtracting.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Adding the stopping energy to the photon energy.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing photon energy from the number of photons arriving each second.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Brighter light gives each emitted electron more energy.

dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires linking mostly small deflections to the small size of the nucleus.
dhs-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Scattering reveals the internal arrangement of nucleons.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Requires recalling the order of magnitude of an atomic diameter.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires comparing both the spread and the distance from the accepted value.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Closely grouped readings must be accurate.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires combining weight and drag using the velocity at the top of the trajectory.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Zero vertical velocity means zero vertical acceleration.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires reading the lift’s free-body diagram and interpreting zero resultant force.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the impulses needed for the same speed change with two different masses.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Using the braking time for one load as the difference.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires identifying which wires carry the full force and which share it.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Adding the two extensions of parallel wires.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the perpendicular separation of the forces in a couple.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Using the card’s width as the moment arm.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires calculating the gain in gravitational potential energy and converting days to seconds.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing total loading work from recoverable elastic energy.

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish the speeds at the two positions and combine energy conservation with the radial force equation.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Using the angular speed at the top in the bottom force equation

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Students must connect a stationary point on the potential graph with cancellation of the two field vectors.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Adding gravitational field magnitudes without considering direction

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Students must recognise the displacement–velocity ellipse with the axes in an unfamiliar order.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing a phase plot with a time plot

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must connect increased drag with the height and width of the resonance peak.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Treating increased damping as a change in the natural frequency

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Students must link the squared voltage ratio, the inverse area ratio and the square root for diameter.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Treating cross-sectional area as proportional to diameter

dhs-2024-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Students must interpret the null reading and use the uniform wire as a potential divider.
dhs-2024-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Using the length of the wire beyond the sliding contact

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Students must compare the closeness of each mean to the true value and the spread within each set.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students apply Newton's second law once at terminal speed and once before force balance.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Using the drag force alone as the resultant force

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students must translate a falling speed into a decreasing slope on the distance graph.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Copying speed or acceleration directly onto a distance graph

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Students must connect the pressure gradient with upthrust and the force balance for floating ice.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Students must combine moment balance with Hooke's law and isolate the change in spring compression.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Reporting total compression instead of extra compression

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must match the directions of the forces and check that the vector triangle closes.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming every triangular arrangement of arrows represents zero net force

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The work calculation is direct once students convert both the area and the stroke length to SI units.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Applying a length conversion factor directly to an area

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Students must calculate the energy gained in lifting the water and convert one day to seconds before finding power.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Omitting the gravitational energy gain per kilogram

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students need only convert the one-hour period to seconds and use the angular speed to find tip speed.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the second hand's period for the minute hand

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The question links the stars’ shared period to their angular velocity and orbital speeds.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Equal angular velocity implies equal linear speed.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must balance two inverse-square forces and solve for the distance from Earth.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using the Earth-to-Moon mass ratio in the final denominator.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must scale gravitational potential with distance and take the signed difference.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing work by gravity with external work.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must apply the first law to rapid compression with negligible heat transfer.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming a temperature rise requires heat input.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must connect the decaying amplitude to the oscillator’s energy.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing the damping force with the restoring force.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must find the spherical spreading area before calculating the power intercepted by the ear.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the area of a circle for radiation in all directions.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must evaluate Malus’ law at three angles and rank the resulting intensities.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming transmitted intensity falls as the angle increases from 0° to 180°.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must recall the fixed-end fundamental and use its integer multiples.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Treating the string length as one full fundamental wavelength.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must compute the second-order angle, bound the highest order and count both sides of the pattern.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Doubling the diffraction angle or omitting the central maximum.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must infer equal charge-to-mass ratios from equilibrium and use the change in field to compare accelerations.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: A larger electric force implies a larger acceleration even when mass scales with charge.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must scale the resistance by both length and width before adding the two resistances.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Accounting for length while overlooking the change in cross-sectional area.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must infer both the polarity and the doubled frequency of the force graph from the two currents.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming the force follows the sign and period of one current.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must infer the magnetic force direction from the perspective diagram and balance moments using different lever arms.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must establish equal speeds before applying the mass-to-charge scaling for the radius.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Treating the bending radius as proportional to charge.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must account for the turns ratio twice when relating the primary current to the fixed load.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Applying the turns ratio once while holding the secondary current fixed.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Calculate the photon energy and match it to a gap on the diagram.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Using an energy level as the photon energy

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Convert the energy to joules, find the momentum and apply the uncertainty relation.

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Compare the penetration of the emissions and the persistence of the half-lives.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assuming relative penetrating ability guarantees detection

dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Convert the binding energies per nucleon to total binding energies.
dhs-2025-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Using binding energy per nucleon as total binding energy

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Straightforward weighted sum of percentage uncertainties.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the powers

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that shifting the graph down changes both net area and absolute area.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Assuming distance is unchanged because the graph shapes are identical

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Area under a linear force–extension graph between two points.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using $Fx$ instead of $\tfrac{1}{2}Fx$ for elastic energy

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs careful free-body analysis of separate bodies and Newton's laws.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Equating zero resultant force with being at rest

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Standard result that acceleration down a frictionless slope is independent of mass.

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Whole-system acceleration then Newton's second law on one block.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Taking the force on the 2.0 kg block as the applied force minus friction

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Single Newton's second law equation at the top of a vertical circle.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Adding weight to the centripetal force instead of subtracting

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Vector addition of three point-mass fields at the centroid of an equilateral triangle.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Combining two fields at 120° as if they were at 60° (getting $\sqrt{3}$)

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Scalar sum of potentials plus recognising potential has no direction.

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Ignoring the period change or not squaring ω

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Must halve for unpolarised light, then apply Malus' law twice using angle differences between successive axes.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using the absolute axis angles instead of the angle between successive polariser axes

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Two proportional reasoning steps: intensity proportional to amplitude squared, then power conserved over a smaller area.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Treating intensity as proportional to amplitude rather than amplitude squared

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Direct use of the Rayleigh criterion and small-angle geometry with large powers of ten.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Inverting the ratio (dividing distance by angle) or using radius instead of diameter

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming r.m.s. speed is proportional to temperature

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that connected containers share a common pressure, then comparing V/T.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Ignoring that the pressure is equal in connected containers, or mishandling the V/T ratio

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs an energy budget to decide that not all the ice melts, then compute the mass melted.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming all ice melts or confusing 0 K with 0 °C

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs to combine $I = nAvq$ with $N = nAL$ so that the unknown area cancels.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Not realising the cross-sectional area cancels; using number density instead of total number

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Must combine the half-power rule for sinusoidal a.c. with the effect of half-wave rectification.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring that the diode blocks half of each cycle

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Parallel combination plus internal resistance; routine calculation.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Forgetting the internal resistance or adding the resistors in series

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Must trace each circuit to find the potential range between X and Y as the slider moves.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming any potentiometer arrangement gives a range starting from zero

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Must identify the series pair across the battery and share the voltage inversely with capacitance.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Sharing voltage in proportion to capacitance rather than inversely

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires two ideas: equal and opposite forces (Newton's third law) and attraction for parallel currents.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking the wire with larger current exerts or feels a larger force

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Chained calculation: field, acceleration, time in plates, then deflection, plus direction reasoning.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using the plate separation as the distance travelled or reversing the force direction for a positive charge

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Coulomb's law ratio with a small trap in reading 'adding 3Q'.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Reading 'adding 3Q' as making the charge 3Q, or forgetting to square the distance

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Simple recognition that the field is unchanged while the perpendicular area decreases.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Confusing magnetic flux density with magnetic flux

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct application of Faraday's law with flux linkage.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the number of turns

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Recall $E = hc/\lambda$ and recognise the linear graph against $1/\lambda$.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking photon energy increases with wavelength

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Forgetting to square the well width

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Unfamiliar twist: mass lost is only the escaping alpha particles, not the decayed nuclei.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Equating the mass lost with the fraction of nuclei decayed

dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Recall of penetrating power of alpha, beta and gamma radiation.
dhs-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Mixing up the penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Compare the spread and the offset from the actual value separately.

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Apply the percentage uncertainty rule to a quotient with a squared variable.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Forgetting to double the uncertainty contribution of the squared speed

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Use the velocity to infer how the displacement graph’s gradient changes.

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Infer both displacements from the staircase and solve for the launch angles.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming both trajectory solutions are above the horizontal

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Find the sand’s rate of momentum gain and add its contribution to the driving force.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming constant belt speed means no extra force

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Use the first force balance to establish the drag coefficient and then set up the second balance.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Treating total drag as additional driving force

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Use the rope constraint to find each displacement before applying energy conservation.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Using the initial separation as each object’s displacement

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Recall how increasing fluid pressure with depth produces upthrust.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing the magnitude of upthrust with its physical origin

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Combine force balance in two directions with a moment balance about the cable attachment.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Comparing force magnitudes without resolving components

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Use the geometry of the stretched cord before applying energy conservation.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing draw length with total cord extension

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must compare angular displacements in an Earth-centred frame and identify the first repeat alignment.

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must find the common angular speed at one radius and use it at the other.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Using the same centripetal acceleration at both radii

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify the spacecraft's instantaneous velocity when the net force becomes zero.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming an orbit persists without centripetal force

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must derive the inverse square-root dependence and apply it to the new radius.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing the radius dependence of force with that of orbital speed

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must infer velocity from displacement and square it to get the kinetic-energy graph.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing kinetic energy with displacement or potential energy

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The direction of a damping force is a direct recall point.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing damping with the restoring force

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must calculate wavelength and convert a fraction of it to a phase difference.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Using the wrong phase angle for one wavelength

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must recognise the inverse dependence of the minimum resolvable angle on slit width.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming a narrower slit gives a smaller resolvable angle

ejc-2017-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must convert the line density to grating spacing before using the second-order condition.
ejc-2017-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Using line density as the slit separation

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must express pressure and density in base units and combine them to obtain speed units.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Choosing a formula without checking dimensional homogeneity

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must propagate absolute uncertainty through a difference and fractional uncertainty through products and powers.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Subtracting absolute uncertainties when subtracting measurements

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must track whether velocity increases or decreases using the sign of the acceleration.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing maximum acceleration with maximum velocity

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must relate the height ratio to the vertical speeds and distinguish vertical motion from horizontal motion.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Assuming flight time scales directly with maximum height

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must infer the shared acceleration from the trailer's forces and apply it to the car.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing the trailer's net force or tow force with the car's net force

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must conserve horizontal momentum and use the combined mass after impact.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Including vertical impact momentum in the horizontal calculation

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Apply Hooke’s law to each spring and add the extensions.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Treating series springs as sharing the load.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Replace the two weights by a single resultant and apply rotational equilibrium.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Using one weight’s line of action for both weights.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Use conservation of energy to eliminate mass and compare the squared speeds.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming height is proportional to speed.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Find the fall time before dividing the energy transferred by that time.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing the duration of free fall with an expression proportional to $1/g$.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Recognise how reducing damping changes the resonance curve.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming that less damping lowers the resonance peak.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Identify which actual force supplies the inward acceleration.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Drawing centripetal force as an extra force.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Resolve lift into two components and eliminate the unknown mass and lift.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Swapping the horizontal and vertical lift components.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Distinguish properties fixed by the orbit from energies that also depend on mass.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming satellites in the same orbit have the same energies.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Use the inverse-radius potential and distinguish potential from potential energy.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Reversing the sign of the external work.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Translate the separation into a phase difference and apply it to both displacement and motion.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Reversing displacement without reversing transverse velocity.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Combine the squared amplitude factor with the linear area factor.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Treating wave intensity as proportional to amplitude.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Recognise the definition of the principle of superposition.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Identify which change increases the double-slit fringe spacing.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming wider slit separation gives wider fringe spacing.

ejc-2018-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Estimate the angular separation and use the Rayleigh criterion with a visible wavelength.
ejc-2018-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Treating physical separation as angular separation.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Estimate the scaled radius and match it to a familiar object.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Comparing a calculated radius with an object’s diameter.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must combine reading variation with the meter’s percentage accuracy.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Using half the observed range alone.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must square the speed ratio before substituting into a constant-acceleration equation.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Using the speed ratio as a ratio of squared speeds.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must interpret dot spacing as speed and relate changes in spacing to the track profile.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Reading equal-time dot spacing as acceleration.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must combine horizontal kinematics with energy conservation and recognise the kinetic energy at the apex.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming the projectile stops at the highest point.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the student chooses the two blocks pulled by the specified string.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Including blocks on the wrong side of the string.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must resolve tension in two directions and convert the resulting angle to the vertical.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Reporting the angle to the horizontal.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must subtract momentum vectors by recognising that only the vertical component reverses.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Treating equal momentum magnitudes as equal vectors.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a constant speed from a constant velocity when checking equilibrium.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming constant speed guarantees zero resultant force.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must convert the pressure difference into a force and distinguish upthrust from net force.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must use vertical equilibrium and moment balance before converting from the pivot to the requested reference point.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Reporting the distance from an axle instead of from the van’s front.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must recognise that the launch point and P have the same height and account for energy dissipated by friction.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Using the depth of the dip as the net height change.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must infer the drag coefficient from maximum speed and use two different speed laws at the lower speed.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming constant engine power means constant thrust.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must identify which speed is equal at the point of contact and apply the radius ratio in the correct direction.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Equating angular speeds at the point of contact.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the limiting tension at the top and use that condition in an energy balance.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming the bob can reach the top with zero speed while the string stays taut.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must combine the gravitational and centripetal force equations, then convert both orbital data to SI units.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Using kilometres or hours directly with the SI value of G.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Symmetry determines the graph at its midpoint.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must compare both orbital energies and angular velocities.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Comparing potential energies from radius alone

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Three related quantities must be distinguished by their sign and dependence on radius.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Dropping the sign of the potential change

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The defining acceleration condition singles out the bouncing ball.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Two simultaneous equations determine the amplitude and angular frequency before the final substitution.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the potential-energy coefficient and convert it to a period.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q22.misconception: Dropping the half in the energy expression

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the percentage reduction and use the periodicity of Malus’ law.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Using the fraction lost as the fraction transmitted

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: One wavelength calculation and a phase conversion are needed.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Ignoring phase equivalence modulo one cycle

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Recognizing Huygens’ principle identifies the source of the fringes.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must select the correct spot row and order and combine geometry with the grating equation.

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Different end conditions determine the two independent mode numbers.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Using the same harmonic series for both tubes

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students read both voltages at the same current and add them.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming equal potential differences in series

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The only steps are finding the charge per revolution and converting angular frequency to period.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Treating angular frequency as revolutions per second

ejc-2019-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The same network must be redrawn for two different terminal pairs.
ejc-2019-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Keeping the same branches when the terminals change

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Matching units in each term identifies both quantities directly.

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must propagate uncertainty through a quotient and recognise that dividing by four preserves relative uncertainty.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Dividing the percentage uncertainty by the number of layers

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the calibration axes and distinguish a constant offset from a scale error.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming every systematic error is a constant offset

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must connect acceleration to the changing slope of displacement and compare the signed acceleration areas.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Treating zero acceleration as zero velocity

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must recognise that the released spanner inherits the elevator’s velocity in the floor frame.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming a released object starts at rest in every frame

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must identify the common tension and take the inverse ratio of the spring constants.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Taking extension as directly proportional to spring constant

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must choose a common level within the mercury and account for two liquids on the oil side.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Ignoring the oil column or the interface height difference

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must combine opposite pairs and then add the remaining forces as vectors.

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must apply Newton’s laws to the pair of blocks and then to one block.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Using the mass of the other block as the total mass

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must compute the air mass flow rate before applying the momentum principle.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing mass flow rate with thrust

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must isolate the relevant force–time area and add the resulting velocity change.

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must track the signs of momentum and conserve the sum of the two kinetic energies.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Letting kinetic energies cancel because velocities are opposite

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student needs to identify a Newton’s third-law force pair and distinguish it from forces on the crate.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Thinking acceleration makes a third-law pair unequal

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must account for the reversed axes and identify the work recovered on unloading.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Reading area below the curve when force is on the horizontal axis

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must calculate useful power, infer input power from efficiency and subtract.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Applying the wasted fraction to the useful output power

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must recognise that the angular speed is shared across latitudes and translate direct proportionality into a graph.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing common angular speed with common linear speed

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must compare velocity directions and account for the change in height.

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must read both distances and add the two fields in the correct direction.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Subtracting fields that point in the same direction

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must estimate a local tangent using a secant that straddles the point.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Using a one-sided slope for a curved graph

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must read the potentials and use the correct sign for external work.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Confusing external work with work done by gravity

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish mass-dependent orbital energy from quantities set by Earth's rotation.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q21.misconception: Confusing gravitational potential with potential energy

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must read the two intercepts and convert angular frequency to period.

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must choose the correct starting phase and distinguish the second crossing from the first.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Using the first crossing of the target position

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must track the light's polarisation direction after the first filter.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Using the vertical as the incident polarisation reference

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must infer particle velocity from the motion of the wave profile and distinguish it from acceleration.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Reading particle motion directly from the slope without accounting for wave direction

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must count intervals between compressions before applying the wave equation.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q26.misconception: Counting compressions instead of the gaps between them

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must infer the phase relation from the central minimum and count successive fringes.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming the two sources are in phase

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must use both observations to distinguish the change in screen distance from its final value.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q28.misconception: Confusing final distance or fringe spacing with its change

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must apply the angular resolution criterion and estimate a visible wavelength.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing the minimum resolvable angle with a minimum distance

ejc-2020-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must scale the sine of the angle with order and then find the angular separation.
ejc-2020-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Assuming diffraction angle is proportional to order

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must estimate a cube's edge length and count how many fit along all three dimensions.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Comparing linear dimensions instead of volumes

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Both terms under the square root must be matched to the units of speed squared.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Matching terms to the units of speed instead of speed squared

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must propagate two fractional uncertainties through a cubic dependence and round the result.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Omitting the factor of three in the diameter uncertainty

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must connect the shapes of three time graphs to terminal velocity.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Assuming displacement levels off at terminal velocity

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the flight time from horizontal motion and use it to find the vertical displacement.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Treating the wall as the point of maximum height

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must combine rotational equilibrium of the rod with vertical force balance on each object.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Equating weight with string tension in a liquid

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must recognise constant free-fall acceleration followed by an acceleration reversal when the parachute opens.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming acceleration must point in the direction of motion

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must include both masses in the downslope component while using only the block’s friction limit.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Ignoring the downslope force transmitted by the sphere

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must find the common speed and distinguish each particle’s momentum and kinetic energy from the totals.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Applying the speed-squared factor to momentum

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must calculate thrust from momentum flow and then account for weight in the helicopter’s force balance.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Treating thrust as the resultant force

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must translate piecewise constant force into piecewise constant speed–time gradient.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Copying the force–time graph as the speed–time graph

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student applies one horizontal momentum balance to the initially stationary system.

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student combines Newton’s third law with the downward resultant force on the man.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Treating weight and normal force as a third-law pair

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student identifies which force transfers energy in four different situations.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Reversing which body does work on which

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student reads the useful output and total input from the diagram and applies the efficiency definition.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Using wasted power as the useful output

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: A direct rearrangement of the relation between tangential speed and angular velocity gives the dependence on radius.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing constant tape speed with constant angular velocity

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must resolve two contact forces and solve simultaneous component equations.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Equating friction with the net centripetal force

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must combine the orbital force equation with the period relation and isolate the scaling.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Keeping the orbiting mass in the period formula

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must track the force sign and identify the body on which each force acts.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Dropping the minus sign in the force–energy relation

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must infer the potential at Q and use the signed potential difference.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Using the final potential in place of the potential difference

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must infer the period and eliminate the unknown orbital radius.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q21.misconception: Confusing orbital radius with orbital speed

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must select a sine solution and substitute one eighth of a cycle.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q22.misconception: Using the phase angle itself as the sine factor

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must identify the energy repeat time and double it before calculating angular frequency.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Equating the kinetic-energy period with the displacement period

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must read the crest-to-trough separation in wavelengths and convert it to phase.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing the number of wavelengths with the number of half-turns

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must identify which pattern survives when orthogonal polarisation suppresses interference.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Treating crossed polarizers on separate slits as crossed filters in series

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must calculate the wavelength and count the compression intervals in the diagram.

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student needs to identify the nodes and track the phase reversal across each one.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming every point outside P’s segment is in antiphase

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must model the flight path as an interference screen and convert spatial separation into time.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q28.misconception: Confusing fringe spacing with the separation of the sources

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must choose the shortest visible wavelength and convert the angular limit to a linear separation.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Using a longer wavelength to find the minimum separation

ejc-2021-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must transfer the wavelength from the grating equation to the double-slit equation and cancel the grating spacing.
ejc-2021-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Using the grating spacing as the double-slit separation

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must estimate the helium mass from its nucleon number and cube the nuclear radius.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Using the atomic radius for the compressed volume
