ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires simplifying a derived unit raised to a fractional power.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Incorrect cancellation of SI base units

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires setting displacement to zero at the end of a vertical round trip.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing total flight time with ascent time

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires identifying which change increases the volume displaced by a fully submerged block.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Upthrust depends on the block’s density

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires splitting the load and reading the extension before calculating the area under the graph.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing total energy from the useful energy a machine delivers.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Requires tracking successive elastic collisions between blocks of equal and unequal masses.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming complete energy transfer between unequal masses

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires combining force balance with moments about the wall contact.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Swapping the lever arms for horizontal and vertical forces

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires using the net inward force on each mass to build up the three tensions.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Equating each tension to the centripetal force of only one mass

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires finding the potential barrier from just the Moon-side area and converting it to a speed.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using the entire field–distance graph to find the barrier

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that gravitational potential energy increases as it becomes less negative.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Treating gravitational potential energy as a positive inverse-radius quantity

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires converting both temperatures to kelvin and using the square-root dependence of r.m.s. speed.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Using Celsius in a kinetic-theory ratio

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires identifying how vessel volume affects the slope of the pressure–temperature graph.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Treating volume as a pressure offset

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting the piston stroke and relating loss of contact to peak downward acceleration.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires doubling the crest-to-trough distance before converting a spatial separation into a phase difference.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Taking crest-to-trough distance as one wavelength

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires converting line density to grating spacing and checking which orders can exist at violet wavelengths.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming higher diffraction orders are impossible for violet light

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must select the limiting colour and apply the angular resolution criterion.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must combine the equipotential condition with the inverse-square field law.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming connected spheres have equal charge.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must reverse the field relative to the force on a negative charge and resolve the diagonal field.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must track how a parallel branch affects voltage division and total power.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating the voltage across the parallel branch as fixed.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must identify the balance span that corresponds to each resistor.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the full 80 cm for the second resistor.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must combine polarity reversal with damping from the loaded coil.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must project the field, account for the flux reversal and use Faraday’s law to find charge.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using only the initial flux change.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must identify a full period and time-average the square of a non-sinusoidal current.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Averaging the signed current before finding power.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the effects of intensity and frequency on photoemission.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Confusing photon energy with photon arrival rate.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must connect the X-ray cutoff to the full electron energy and interpret the logarithmic slope.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Treating an inverse relation as curved on log–log axes.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must convert the stated percentage precision into an absolute momentum spread.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Using full momentum in place of its uncertainty.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must remove the background before applying decay and restore it for the meter reading.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Applying decay to the background count.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must compare the reactant and product masses and convert the rest-energy increase to electronvolts.
ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Equating the rest-energy increase with the stationary-target threshold.

ejc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must apply the changes in proton and neutron number twice and read the grid.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must express pressure and density in SI base units and take the square root.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Assigning the units of the full expression to the constant.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Subtracting two velocity vectors requires constructing a triangle and converting its angle to a bearing.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Reversing the order of relative velocity subtraction.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Compare each mean with the reference value and each range with the other ranges.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing closeness to the true value with agreement among repeated readings.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Identify when the gap stops shrinking and calculate two areas under the graph.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing the distance closed with the remaining separation.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Use the slope as velocity and recognize its reversal on each bounce.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Reading the height–time graph as a speed–time graph.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Set up a ratio of free-fall equations and take its square root.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Treating fall time as directly proportional to distance divided by acceleration.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Identify which bodies the two stated forces act on.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Treating centripetal force as an additional interaction.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Newton’s second law gives the requested rate directly from the stated force.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Confusing momentum change with its rate.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Resolve the velocity and account for the reversal of its perpendicular component.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Using the component parallel to the wall or omitting the rebound.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Compare pressures using a shared depth in the connected liquid.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming equal pressures at the same height across different liquids.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Locate the common intersection of the force lines and distinguish the third-law pair.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Selecting the force exerted by the wall on the beam.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Use the total drop for energy and the compression distance for the spring’s work.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Using only the fall before contact to calculate the loss of gravitational potential energy.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Infer the drag at the initial speed, scale it, and combine three forces on the slope.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming the same engine force at constant power.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Find the final speed and include both energy gains in the efficiency.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Counting only the gain in gravitational potential energy.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Identify the individual forces and recognize their centripetal resultant.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Drawing the centripetal resultant as an extra force.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Use the squared angular speed to infer curvature and compare accelerations at two radii.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming centripetal acceleration increases linearly with angular speed.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: It requires separate radial force balances for the two masses.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Treating each string tension as the net force

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: It requires finding both source distances and adding the two field contributions.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Confusing gravitational force with field strength

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing gravitational potential from gravitational potential energy.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: It links the SHM speed profile to the time spent in each region.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming equal distances take equal times in SHM

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: It requires combining the force balance with the maximum downward acceleration in SHM.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: It requires counting the distance in a full cycle and solving for the remaining fraction.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: It requires identifying an equivalent phase point and interpreting half-amplitude on a sinusoid.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing the phase of Q with the phase difference

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: It requires using the direction of propagation to infer particle velocity and using displacement to infer acceleration.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing wave motion with particle motion

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: It requires counting wavelengths from compressions and applying the wave equation.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: It requires holding intensity fixed while scaling power and distance.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: It requires relating the pipe boundary conditions to the fundamental and higher resonances.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Allowing even harmonics in a tube closed at one end

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: It requires comparing the spacing of the incoming and outgoing wavefronts.

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: It requires inferring the source phase relation and counting maxima from the central minimum.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Using the in-phase condition for antiphase sources

ejc-2022-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: It requires using the sine limit to find the maximum order and counting both sides of the centre.
ejc-2022-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing maximum order with total number of images

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: It requires subtracting the car velocity as a vector and judging the direction of the resultant.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Reversing the order of relative-velocity subtraction

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must eliminate flight time using the horizontal and vertical equations.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Giving a downward displacement a positive sign

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The two force equations require consistent positive directions before eliminating the shared acceleration.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assigning independent acceleration directions to connected blocks

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must use both momentum components to find the unknown speed.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Conserving speed instead of vector momentum

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must extend the force lines and determine the sense of the hinge reaction.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming the hinge reaction is normal to the beam

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The two graph shapes follow from substituting the free-fall displacement into the energy equation.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating free-fall displacement as proportional to time

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must infer the resistance coefficient from accelerating motion and use it at a new steady speed.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Equating driving and resistive forces while the car accelerates

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must resolve the normal force along two axes to eliminate it.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Using the whole normal force as the centripetal force

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must use the diagram to find the height gain, then combine energy conservation and radial dynamics.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Equating the rod force to the net centripetal force

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must identify the zero-pressure intercepts and relate their ratio to absolute temperature.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Taking ratios of temperature intervals as ratios of absolute temperatures

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The calculation uses the ideal gas law before and after opening the tap at the same temperature.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Averaging the initial pressures and volumes

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student can substitute directly after recognising the density in the kinetic-theory equation.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Omitting the one-third factor in the pressure equation

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must express melting as a power and eliminate the common heat-loss rate.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Treating all heater energy as latent heat

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must apply the first law to the contents while tracking net heating and mechanical work.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Counting the refrigerator motor’s work as work on the contents

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must identify the initial phase and differentiate twice with the correct signs.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Using sine when the initial displacement is maximal

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must track which part of an asymmetric pulse reaches the fixed end first and how its displacement changes on reflection.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Reversing the arrival order as well as inverting the pulse

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Students must extend the wave profile and infer the particle velocity from a shift of the profile.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing wave motion with particle motion

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Students must convert a path difference to a phase relation and intensities to amplitudes.

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Students must combine the small-angle diffraction relation with the change in peak intensity.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Assuming peak intensity scales linearly with slit width

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: One application of the double-slit formula gives the required inverse scaling.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Scaling screen distance directly with wavelength

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Students must use the initial equilibrium to eliminate the unknown electric force before applying Newton’s second law.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the doubled electric force as the net force

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Students must find the common current and account for both leads when calculating voltage and power losses.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Ignoring losses in one or both supply wires

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Students must reduce a nested resistor network and apply voltage division twice.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing terminal voltage with branch voltage

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must resolve the velocity relative to the field and use the magnetic force equation.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Multiplying by the sine instead of dividing when solving for speed

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must track how much of each coil is inside the field and distinguish linkage from its rate of change.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Treating the largest flux linkage as the largest induced current

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Students compare voltage-squared and resistance factors once they recognise that frequency does not enter the power expression.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Treating frequency as a factor in resistive power

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students convert the speed uncertainty to a momentum uncertainty and use it to estimate the minimum position uncertainty.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Using velocity uncertainty directly in the uncertainty relation

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Students must interpret logarithmic slopes and reason about how two decay contributions change relative to each other.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assuming the shorter-lived nuclide dominates at late times

ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Students identify the standard inference from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering results.
ejc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing evidence for a nucleus with evidence for electron energy levels

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Students estimate two familiar dimensions and multiply them by the known length.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Underestimating or overestimating the cross-sectional area

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students distinguish random error, systematic error and fractional uncertainty when comparing measurement procedures.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing longer timing intervals with averaging at fixed instrument uncertainty

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: It requires selecting and rearranging one constant-acceleration equation.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Using a constant final speed to estimate travel time.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: It requires finding the fall time before calculating the horizontal distance.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: It requires matching the release position, initial velocity and acceleration to the graph.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Students must account for opposing weights and the combined inertia of the two masses.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Adding the opposing weights as driving forces.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Students must conserve signed momentum and use the loss of kinetic energy to eliminate choices.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Treating inelastic collisions as perfectly inelastic.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: It requires equating the change in upthrust to the removed weight and relating displaced volume to all four cylinders.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Using the cross-sectional area of just one cylinder.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Students must read the moment arms and distinguish the change in reaction from the final reaction.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Reporting the final reaction as the change.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The main step is identifying extension as the stretched length minus the natural length.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Using total length in Hooke’s law.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Students must combine quadratic energy growth in free fall with the approach to terminal speed under drag.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming kinetic energy rises linearly with time in free fall.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Students must relate mass to both orbital radius and string extension at fixed speed.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Treating the stretched length as the extension.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Students must resolve weight in opposite radial directions and compare two tension equations.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Equating the rope tension with the centripetal force.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: It requires taking a square root after forming the inverse-square ratio.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming gravitational field strength varies inversely with distance.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Students must connect gravity to circular orbital motion and distinguish kinetic energy, total energy and period.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming every equatorial orbit is geostationary.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: It asks students to recognize the defining property of a uniform field.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing uniform field strength with uniform potential.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Students must infer the motion’s period and phase from a kinetic-energy graph and calculate the velocity amplitude.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Using the kinetic-energy period as the oscillation period.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must project circular motion onto the floor and track whether the shadow reverses.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing final displacement with distance travelled

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must identify the effect of reduced damping on the resonance curve.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Expecting reduced damping to flatten the resonance peak

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must project the ear separation along the wave direction before calculating phase.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q21.misconception: Using ear separation directly as path difference

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The calculation is direct once the student reads a full cycle from each graph.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must read the angle reference in the diagram before matching the transmission graph.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Treating the marked angle as the angle between transmission axes

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must connect a horizontal movement to the length changes in both arms.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q24.misconception: Counting only one arm of the sliding tube

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must relate the open tube’s fundamental to successive resonances of an air column closed by water.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Using the same end conditions for both tubes

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must infer the fixed amplitude pattern from a single snapshot of the two moving waves.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q26.misconception: Identifying a node from one component’s instantaneous zero

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must combine stationary-wave spacing, the detection rate and a speed conversion.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Equating adjacent maxima spacing to one wavelength

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must convert line density to spacing, find the highest possible order and count both sides.

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The wavelength ratio follows from equating the order–wavelength products at the same angle.
ejc-2023-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Taking wavelength proportional to order at fixed angle

ejc-2023-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must equate the small-angle separation to the Rayleigh limit and estimate a visible wavelength.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must cancel the length units and express power as current times potential difference.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Ignoring the squared current in dimensional analysis

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must use the velocity sign, the effect of drag and the equal ascent and descent distances.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Plotting speed when the graph asks for velocity

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must eliminate time before applying the speed and height ratios.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating time of fall as directly proportional to height

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: You must track contact forces on two blocks and use Newton’s third law.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating a contact force as the applied force.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The calculation requires subtracting the block’s weight from the upthrust before applying Newton’s second law.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using upthrust as the resultant force.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: You must combine two radial force equations with conservation of energy and interpret the sign of the normal force.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming that the normal force must point inward.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: You must interpret force as the gradient of the kinetic-energy graph.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Mistaking decreasing positive force for decreasing kinetic energy.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: You must infer GM from surface gravity and then evaluate the potential at the new radius.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Using altitude as the distance from the centre.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The period scaling is straightforward once both heights are converted to orbital radii.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using heights instead of orbital radii.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: You must convert the amplitude to metres and square the angular frequency.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using angular frequency without squaring it.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: You must infer damping from the decay curves and then predict the resonance response.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Giving the more damped oscillator a taller resonance peak.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: You must eliminate the latent-heat term from two power balances with a common heat loss.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Equating the difference in heater powers to heat loss.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: You must read the compression work from a pressure–volume diagram and apply the first law over a cycle.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Adding compression and expansion work magnitudes.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: You must apply Malus’ law twice and identify the angle between the last two axes.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Measuring the final angular difference from the wrong polariser.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: You must convert the lens diameter and then turn the limiting angle into a linear separation.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing angular resolution with linear separation.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: You must find the smallest pair of matching diffraction orders before calculating the angle.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the same nonzero order for both wavelengths.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: You must identify which resistor is referenced to zero and evaluate the two resistance limits.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Taking the voltage across the fixed resistor.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: You must check the diode direction and determine which divider branch gains voltage as temperature falls.
ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Connecting the heater across the fixed resistor.

ejc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires superposing two signed potential-energy contributions and reversing the resulting change.

hci-2024-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish what intensity controls from what photon energy controls.

hci-2024-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must convert photon energy to electronvolts and match it to a level difference.
hci-2024-other-p1-q28.misconception: Using an absolute energy level in place of an energy difference

hci-2024-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must convert per-nucleon values to total binding energies and account for both deuterium nuclei.
hci-2024-other-p1-q29.misconception: Counting nucleons in only one reactant nucleus

hci-2024-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must subtract the background from both readings before applying the two-half-life reduction.
hci-2024-other-p1-q30.misconception: Applying decay to the total detector reading

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: A familiar size estimate and the formula for a sphere’s volume suffice.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Underestimating how much volume changes with radius

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The graph can be selected by checking its initial slope and turning point.

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The question combines momentum conservation, Newton’s third law and the condition for an elastic collision.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using contact time to decide whether a collision is elastic

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must combine equal spring extensions with two moment equations that include the rule’s weight.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Omitting the weight of the metre rule

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Recognising floating equilibrium reduces the problem to calculating the cube’s weight.

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must locate the intersection of two lines of action and use force balance to choose the arrow direction.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating the wall force as purely horizontal

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student differentiates the potential energy and interprets the force’s sign.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Dropping the minus sign in the force–potential energy relation

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must resolve the normal force using the cone’s angle to the vertical, then take a ratio.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Swapping the radial and vertical components of the normal force

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish gravitational field strength from free-fall acceleration measured relative to the rotating Earth.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Ignoring Earth’s rotation in apparent free fall

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must track the radius dependence and sign of two orbital energies.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Treating a less negative potential energy as a decrease

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must convert the molar mass ratio into a density ratio and take its square root.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using an inverse linear dependence of rms speed on density

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish work from heat transfer and distinguish temperature from internal energy.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Assuming internal energy decreases only through cooling

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must find the gas force from the piston’s net force before calculating work.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using net force instead of the gas force to calculate work

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must extract the period and peak velocity from a graph and use them to calculate peak force.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Reading a peak’s time coordinate as the period

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must reverse the full time sequence to get the instantaneous shape of a right-moving pulse.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Copying a time trace directly as a spatial profile

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must account for the first sheet halving unpolarised intensity before applying Malus’ law to the second sheet.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Applying Malus’ law directly to the unpolarised incident intensity

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: It combines the resolution criterion with the small-angle approximation.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Incorrect conversion of aperture or wavelength

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: It requires finding the subset of tube modes that retain a node at the microphone.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming every tube resonance has a node at the microphone

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: It requires using the full plate separation to calculate the field before finding the force.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Treating parallel plates as point charges

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: It requires comparing endpoint potentials from both charges while ignoring the shape of each path.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Basing electrostatic work on the route taken

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: It requires reading the slope from the origin to the curve and taking its reciprocal.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the tangent slope as the reciprocal of resistance

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: It requires applying the ideal-diode model to both branches and tracing the voltage drops.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming every ideal diode has zero voltage across it

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: It requires relating changes in the LDR voltage to the required lengths on a balanced slide wire.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Moving the contact in the direction of the component with increased resistance

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: It requires relating the field around a straight wire to the local current direction everywhere on the coil.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Applying the parallel-wire attraction rule to perpendicular wires

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: It requires converting the resistance and length before using the solenoid field equation.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using total turns where turns per metre are required

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: It requires taking the difference of two circular areas in Faraday’s law.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Squaring the radius change to find the area change

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: It requires reading the peak voltage and applying the sinusoidal r.m.s. relation.

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: It requires tracking the independent effects of frequency and intensity on the current–voltage graph.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Treating intensity as energy per photon

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing the short-wavelength cutoff from the intensities of characteristic peaks.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing peak height with characteristic wavelength

hci-2025-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: It tests the standard definition directly.
hci-2025-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing decay constant with activity or half-life

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: It requires matching units across the equation and expanding joules into SI base units.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Leaving a derived unit in a base-unit expression

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The calculation requires vector subtraction and the correct included angle.

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must track the signed area and distinguish slowing down from reversing.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing negative acceleration with negative velocity

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must infer drag from the drawn trajectory and combine it with weight.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Taking acceleration to be along the velocity

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must connect vertical equilibrium and Newton’s third law to a momentum flow rate.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using the mass flow rate as a force

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The main step is assigning opposite signs to the incoming and outgoing velocities.

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Equilibrium fixes the direction of the resultant before comparing the vector triangles.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using cord length to infer tension magnitude

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The calculation uses the full height loss for gravity and only the penetration distance for the ground force.

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The calculation requires the belt tension difference and the linear speed of the wheel rim.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using one belt tension or the belt speed in the power calculation

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must calculate the radial force and combine it with a perpendicular tangential force.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Equating the net force with the centripetal force

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must equate the inverse-square field magnitudes and take a square root.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using a linear distance dependence for gravitational field strength

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish potential, potential energy and the potential gradient at the field null.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Equating zero field with zero potential

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must infer both angular-frequency and amplitude ratios from the graph and combine them in the energy equation.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Ignoring the squared amplitude in the energy of oscillation

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must use extension from natural length for elastic energy and account for gravity when finding oscillation energy.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Using displacement from equilibrium as the spring’s total extension

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must relate a pressure maximum to instantaneous particle displacement and distinguish amplitude from a snapshot value.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Treating a pressure crest as maximum particle displacement

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must double the slider displacement and connect adjacent interference extrema to half a wavelength.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Counting only one side of the sliding tube

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must check whether 440 Hz is an integer harmonic of each string.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming resonance requires the string’s fundamental frequency

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must equate the power during warming and boiling and cancel the common mass.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using the boiling time without the warming rate

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must recognise the density term in the kinetic-theory pressure equation and take a square root.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Dropping the factor of one third in the pressure equation

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must use scalar potential to infer the charge factor and then add the two field magnitudes.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Subtracting fields from opposite charges at their midpoint

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must combine two current equations and use volume conservation to infer the new length.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Holding the current fixed when only the voltage is fixed

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must convert a battery’s charge capacity into available energy before dividing by power.

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must reduce a series-parallel network, then use charge and voltage relationships to work back to one capacitor.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assigning the full branch voltage to one series capacitor

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must use resistor voltage to find power and recognise exponential decay.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing capacitor voltage with resistor power

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must determine the force direction and balance the force magnitudes.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Making the electric force reinforce the magnetic force

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must link acceleration through a voltage to the radius of magnetic circular motion.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Assuming radius is linear in the mass-to-charge ratio

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must identify the perpendicular projection and combine both forces.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Using the angle to the vertical as the angle to the magnetic field

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must identify the accessible levels and check every possible downward transition against the work function.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Counting all accessible transitions as photoelectrically active

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must interpret absorber readings and estimate how many times the source count rate halves.

hci-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must track the nucleon and proton counts through four decays.
hci-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Changing the mass number in beta-minus decay

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must rearrange the equation and express the joule in base units.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Multiplying by temperature to the fourth power when solving for the constant

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must rearrange a vector difference and recognise the correct head-to-tail diagram.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Reversing the direction of the vector difference.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: A single conservation argument resolves the comparison once the direction of launch is distinguished from speed.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating launch direction as a factor in final speed.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The calculation uses a standard kinematics equation and requires isolating the distance in the second interval.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating the next 15 seconds as a new start from rest.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must write a force equation for each block and eliminate the tension.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Treating the hanging block as if it were in free fall.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: A one-dimensional momentum equation gives the common velocity once signs are assigned.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Adding the magnitudes of opposing momenta.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The calculation requires relating the given displaced weight to upthrust before using seawater density.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing displaced weight with displaced mass.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must find two different extensions under the same force and sum the stored energies.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming springs in series have the same extension.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must find both vertical height changes and include both masses in the final kinetic energy.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Counting only one box in the system’s kinetic energy.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Doubling the radius changes both its value in the centripetal force equation and the extension that sets the tension.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using the stretched length in Hooke’s law.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the speed from energy conservation, then identify the net radial force at the bottom.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Equating the normal force to the centripetal force.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must interpret a more negative potential and multiply the potential change by the satellite’s mass.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing gravitational potential with gravitational potential energy.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must interpret three paths and use both the ideal gas equation and the first law.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming a curved pressure–volume path is adiabatic.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must scale absolute temperature and then apply a square-root relationship for molecular speed.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Scaling Celsius temperature directly or taking rms speed as proportional to temperature.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must identify the energy extrema and recognise where the two energy stores can be equal.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing equilibrium with a turning point.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Two standard SHM relations give the amplitude and acceleration once the period is converted to angular frequency.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing ordinary frequency and angular frequency.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Read the separation as a fraction of a wavelength and calculate the travel time.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using the crossing ahead of Q

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Use the end conditions to find the wavelengths of successive modes.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Rearrange the syllabus resolution formula and interpret the minimum angle.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Treating resolution as independent of wavelength

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Identify the displacement along the electric force and assign the work its sign.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Confusing work by and against the field

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Resolve the entry velocity and apply energy conservation to the component that falls to zero.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using total kinetic energy for motion across the gap

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Calculate the resistance of each material per metre and combine the two paths.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Treating the materials as series resistors

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Trace all four circuits and compare the ammeter currents at the same terminal voltage.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing total current with ammeter current

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Find a direction and speed that let the magnetic force balance the electric force.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Apply the right-hand grip rule for the wire and coil with Lenz's law between them.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Convert the half-wave RMS voltage to peak voltage, scale to the full wire and calculate peak power.
jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the full-sine RMS factor after rectification

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Combine the energy and momentum equations and identify the resulting curve.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Distinguish the voltage-dependent cutoff from lines set by atomic energy gaps.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Remove the background before applying two half-lives and restore it at the end.

jpjc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Balance the mass and proton numbers for beta-minus decay.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Estimate the wire diameter, convert to metres and calculate the area from its radius.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Estimating the clip's size instead of wire thickness

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Links two stages of free fall using the speed at shutter opening.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Resetting the velocity to zero at shutter opening

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: A single momentum balance gives the speed ratio.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the horizontal and vertical components shown by the arrows.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Checking equilibrium along only one axis

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires an energy balance and the distance along the slope.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Treating all lost potential energy as work against friction

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting the scale reading and identifying the inward resultant force.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating apparent weight as the centripetal force

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the zero-normal-force threshold and relating gravitation to the rotation period.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming a nonzero normal force at the threshold of losing contact

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Requires reading the phase from the graph and relating acceleration to displacement.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Putting displacement in phase with acceleration

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing unchanged kinetic energy from unchanged momentum.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming elastic collisions preserve each molecule’s momentum

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Requires linking higher temperature to more frequent momentum transfer to the container walls.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Attributing pressure to collisions between molecules

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Requires finding the fraction of kinetic energy lost and relating it to the temperature rise.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing remaining energy with energy lost

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires projecting the separation onto the propagation direction before finding the phase difference.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Using the separation along the wall as the distance along propagation

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires projecting the amplitude along the antenna and squaring it.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Treating received power as proportional to amplitude

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the full routes and recognising the condition for destructive interference.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Ignoring the path difference before the slits

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires converting the Rayleigh angular limit to a physical spacing at the screen.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing angular separation with physical pixel spacing

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires finding how the electric force changes and using the resulting force imbalance.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming field strength increases with plate separation at fixed voltage

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Resolve the three forces and compare their vertical components.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Identify the cross-section and drift speed before substitution.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Read the diode characteristic and add the resistor drop.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Use earth as the reference and obtain the smaller cell's terminal p.d. from the resistor.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Equating e.m.f. with loaded terminal p.d.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Apply Fleming’s left-hand rule to an inclined field and current into the page.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Link induced e.m.f. to magnetic force and work over a fixed distance.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Find the change in flux linkage between two orientations and divide by time.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Trace the conducting branch and compare the resistance in each half-cycle.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal resistance in both directions

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Combine the turns ratio, equivalent resistance and r.m.s. current.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using peak current for average power

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Identify each term of the photoelectric equation.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Confusing threshold frequency with work function

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Connect electron speed to wavelength and diffraction angle.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming slower electrons have shorter wavelengths

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Map the wavelength ordering to the energy gaps and combine the adjacent transitions.

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Use equal momentum magnitudes to compare the fragments’ kinetic energies.
jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assuming equal momentum implies equal kinetic energy

jpjc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Track the daughters formed while the parent population halves.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Standard base-unit derivation via $V = W/Q$ with $Q = It$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating derived units such as the ohm or coulomb as SI base units

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires reading gradient and sign of a v–t graph rather than any calculation.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Confusing zero acceleration with change of direction

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Two applications of Newton's second law with a changing mass and careful sign handling.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Ignoring direction of acceleration or forgetting the mass changes in the second case

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Single moments equation about one end plus force balance.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Inverting the ratio or neglecting the plank's weight

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Direct Hooke's law with extension computed from lengths.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Equating elastic energy stored to gravitational energy lost by the mass

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Energy bookkeeping with work, friction and GPE on an incline.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using the distance along the slope as the vertical height gain

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: One-step use of $v = r\omega$ with common angular velocity.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking points at different radii on a rigid disc have different periods

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Counter-intuitive result that losing energy increases orbital speed.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming that losing energy to drag makes the satellite slower

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Ratio reasoning with $g \propto 1/r^2$ and $\phi \propto 1/r$, with the height-vs-distance trap.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using height above the surface (3R) instead of distance from Earth's centre (4R)

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Same temperature means same mean KE, giving $v_{rms} \propto 1/\sqrt{m}$.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Combines specific heat and latent heat then divides by power.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Including only one of the two energy stages

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Ideal gas law at constant volume with changing mass and kelvin conversion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using Celsius instead of kelvin temperatures

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Must combine $a_0 = \omega^2x_0$ and $E = \tfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2x_0^2$ with three ratios.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming the same angular frequency for both bodies

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires choosing the cosine form and solving for phase, not assuming linear motion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming the bob moves at constant speed so half the distance takes half the time

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Malus' law with the halving at the first polariser and a percentage decrease to interpret.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Forgetting the first polariser halves unpolarised light, or using cos instead of cos²

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Standard comparison of open–open and closed–open pipe fundamentals.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Mixing up which pipe type has the longer fundamental wavelength

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Must estimate the wavelength of visible light and apply the Rayleigh criterion.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using the aperture size directly or a wrong order of magnitude for light's wavelength

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Must deduce the fixed charge is $-e$, then superpose potentials of opposite sign.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Ignoring the alpha particle's own potential or adding magnitudes regardless of sign

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Must recognise $v + V = E$ and locate the endpoints at $R = r$ and $R = 3r$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Thinking the p.d. across the internal resistance rises with external resistance

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires redrawing a switched network into series and parallel blocks and comparing four configurations.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Closing a switch adds a parallel path, which lowers resistance

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs only $E = \tfrac12 CV^2$ and $mgh$ proportional to it.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming energy stored is proportional to V rather than V²

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Needs $F = BIL\sin\theta$ with the right angle, plus the idea that the magnetic force supplies half the weight.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using cos θ instead of sin θ, or equating the magnetic force to the full weight

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Two standard relations (accelerating p.d. and velocity selector) combined algebraically.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Forgetting to square v = E/B when substituting into the kinetic energy

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must see that the two arm e.m.f.s cancel, despite the motion graph pointing towards a velocity-shaped answer.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Treating the e.m.f. across PQ as proportional to the velocity of the wire

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Direct recall of how a transformer works.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking a transformer passes current through a wire connection or works with d.c.

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Qualitative use of $\Delta y\,\Delta p_y \gtrsim h$ in a standard single-slit context.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking a narrower slit gives a more focused beam

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Recall of electron diffraction plus the link $\lambda = h/(mv)$.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Attributing electron rings to repulsion, or getting the λ–speed trend backwards

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Read a data table against known penetrating powers, allowing for background.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Forgetting to subtract background, so the 301 count with lead looks like gamma

jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs the ratio converted to $N_0/N$ before applying exponential decay with the half-life.
jpjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Treating the daughter-to-parent ratio as the fraction decayed or as the fraction remaining

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The key’s construction requires reversing one vector and adding it tip to tail.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Adding the vector without reversing it

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Recognising how increasing drag changes the velocity–time gradient is the main step.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The solution combines two areas on a force–time graph with the initial momentum.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing change in velocity with final velocity

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The solution requires resolving the two momenta vertically and equating their magnitudes.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Equating momentum magnitudes instead of vertical components

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The calculation requires identifying two perpendicular moment arms about the hip joint.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using the full pivot distance as the moment arm

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The calculation combines displaced-fluid weight with vertical force balance.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The calculation accounts for both the kinetic energy gained and the energy dissipated before finding the final height.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The solution requires finding the horizontal resultant and converting weight to mass before applying Newton’s second law.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Treating the entire supporting force as centripetal

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The solution requires identifying the coefficient of the plotted inverse-square variable.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing the gradient with G alone

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The calculation requires finding the orbital radius and converting the period before using the speed formula.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using altitude as the orbital radius

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The solution combines the molecular kinetic-energy relation with the ideal-gas equation.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing total and mean molecular kinetic energy

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The calculation squares the speed ratio on the Kelvin scale before converting the result to Celsius.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Scaling Celsius temperature or using a linear speed ratio

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation adds the energy absorbed by water and the calorimeter before dividing by the potato mass.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The calculation requires doubling the kinetic-energy period and converting the amplitude to metres.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Using the kinetic-energy period as the oscillation period

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The solution requires recognising how increased damping affects the resonance curve.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming damping changes only the peak height

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The calculation is a direct substitution into Malus’ law.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Recognising reflection and superposition is enough to identify the mechanism.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: A single travelling wave can form a stationary pattern

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: This combines the double-slit fringe-spacing equation with the condition for the second dark fringe.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Counting the second dark fringe as two wavelengths

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: This requires comparing the directions and inverse-square magnitudes of two electric fields.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The calculation requires the direction of the external force and the sign of its work.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the electric force to sign the external work

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: This is a direct substitution into the definition of power.

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The candidate must track how two resistance changes affect the current in the lamp branch.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Treating total current as lamp current

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: This requires relating the direction of the resultant field to the charge velocity.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: A magnetic field always exerts a force on a moving charge

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: This links a stronger magnetic field to a larger balancing moment.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Ignoring the change in balancing moment

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: This requires calculating the coil area and applying Faraday’s law to all turns.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using flux through one turn as the flux linkage

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: This requires finding the secondary rms current and applying the inverse turns ratio to obtain the primary current.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Applying the voltage turns ratio to the current

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: This requires distinguishing the effects of frequency and intensity in the photoelectric effect.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Higher intensity means higher photon energy

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: This combines reading the threshold wavelength with applying the photoelectric equation and converting to electronvolts.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Using a wavelength away from the threshold as the threshold wavelength

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: This requires converting binding energies per nucleon to totals before comparing reactants and products.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Subtracting binding energies per nucleon directly

mi-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Dividing the two activity equations cancels the common number of nuclei and gives the half-life ratio.
mi-2023-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Assuming activity is directly proportional to half-life

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: This requires expressing charge and energy in SI base units and matching exponents.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Matching exponents before accounting for the denominator

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Rearrange the equation and apply the power rule for fractional uncertainties.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Subtracting fractional uncertainties in a quotient.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Identify the zero crossing during the first flight after a bounce.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Treating every zero on a velocity–time graph as a height maximum.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Use the constant-acceleration equation from rest and substitute the Moon’s acceleration.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating fall time as inversely proportional to acceleration.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Find the area of two rectangles, convert impulse to a speed change, then add the initial speed.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing impulse with speed or change in speed with final speed.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Compare moments of equal-size sections to locate the centre of gravity among nearby lines.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming the centre of gravity is at an apparent geometric midpoint.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Set up an equilibrium equation using upthrust, both weights and the spring force.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Ignoring one of the downward forces in equilibrium.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Read the spring constant from the graph and subtract the energies at two loads.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Using one extension or force change in place of the difference between two stored energies.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Compare the friction needed at different radii for the same angular speed.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing angular speed with linear speed.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Find the bob’s speed by energy conservation and then use the radial force equation.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Equating tension alone to the centripetal force.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Compare the two planets using inverse-square scaling and consistent radius units.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using inverse-distance scaling for surface gravity.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Use a ratio of energy changes to infer the signed potential change between Q and R.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Treating a change in energy as a change in potential per unit mass.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Recall that net heating in thermal contact proceeds from higher to lower temperature.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using total internal energy to predict heat flow.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Convert Celsius to kelvin and substitute into the mean energy formula for one atom.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Using Celsius or calculating the energy of the whole sample.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Equate the power during warming and boiling, then eliminate the liquid mass.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing the heating rate with the boiling time or inverting the ratio.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Infer the amplitude and period from consecutive turning points and match both graph intercepts.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Treating the distance or time between opposite turning points as a full amplitude or period.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must recognise the direction of damping.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must convert intensities to amplitudes before combining them.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must count half-wavelengths and nodes for different harmonics.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Excluding the fixed ends when counting nodes

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must combine the syllabus resolution formula with small-angle geometry.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish potential from its local gradient.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Confusing zero potential with zero potential gradient

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must read the diode voltage and calculate the voltage left across the resistor.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Using the supply voltage across one series component

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must identify the null-current branch and apply the driving-loop potential divider.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using the driving emf as the wire voltage

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must infer the magnetic force direction from the original undeflected path.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing magnetic field and magnetic force directions

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must turn the projected-area gradient into a flux-linkage rate.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using flux change without dividing by time

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must chain the voltage ratio, Ohm’s law and equality of power.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must convert a wavelength interval to energy and check several level differences.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Counting levels instead of transition gaps

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must interpret cutoff and peak positions as evidence for two different quantities.

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the total energy release from the photon energy.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Assigning all released energy to the gamma ray

mi-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must connect the beta energy spectrum to two-body decay kinematics.
mi-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Assuming a fixed beta-particle energy share

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Homogeneity check: $\tan\alpha$ is dimensionless, so each term must be too.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Thinking angles in degrees give Q a unit

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Standard terminal-velocity reasoning applied to an acceleration–time graph.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Thinking acceleration levels off at a non-zero value, or confusing a–t with v–t

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Distinguishing kinetic energy conservation overall from what happens during the contact.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Believing kinetic energy is conserved at every instant during an elastic collision

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Needs two Newton's second law equations with the acceleration ratio, then solving simultaneously.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Ignoring friction in one case or doubling the gravity component too

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Needs the upthrust held fixed while the centre of gravity shifts, then the sense of the couple.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming upthrust drops along with the weight

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Needs a force balance on a slope, noting that gravity helps drive the car downhill, before using $P = Fv$.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Ignoring the component of weight along the slope

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Simple efficiency, work and power substitution.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Applying efficiency in the wrong direction or treating weight as mass

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Standard vertical-circle force balance at the top.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Treating tension as the only centripetal force or getting the sign of weight wrong

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Inverse-square ratio, with the trap of using height rather than distance from the centre.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using height above the surface instead of distance from the centre, or thinking orbiting objects are weightless

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Relating loss of PE to work done by the field and the field direction.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing force (E/x) with field strength (E/mx), or reversing the field direction

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Single substitution into the mean KE formula after converting to kelvin; the moles and molar mass are red herrings.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using Celsius temperature or computing the total kinetic energy of the gas instead of per atom

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires recognising equal pressure in connected flasks and combining the volume and temperature ratios.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Ignoring that the connected flasks share the same pressure, or inverting the temperature dependence

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Standard conceptual check of internal energy and the first law.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Equating internal energy with temperature, or treating heat and work as stored quantities

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Resonance condition plus a single speed = distance × frequency step.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Dividing frequency by spacing (or spacing by frequency) instead of multiplying

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Requires knowing that damping lowers the oscillation frequency, which students often ignore for light damping.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Believing damping has no effect on the period, or that the period changes as amplitude decays

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Malus' law with an inverse cosine and the extra step of finding an equivalent angle beyond 180°.

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs $I \propto A^2$ and reading amplitudes off grids while noticing frequency is unchanged.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Thinking amplitude halves when intensity halves, or that frequency changes with intensity

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Direct Rayleigh criterion with a small-angle conversion to separation.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Applying the diffraction angle without multiplying by the object distance, or using radius instead of aperture width

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires vector addition of four fields with careful attention to direction for each charge sign.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Adding field magnitudes without direction, or thinking all like charges give the largest field

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Needs adapting $I = nAvq$ to charge per unit length rather than recall.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating I/e (protons per second) as protons per unit length

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Combines potential-divider reasoning with thermistor behaviour and diode orientation.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Placing the thermistor in the wrong arm of the potential divider or ignoring diode direction

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Chains $I = Q/t$, $V = W/Q$ and the e.m.f. equation, with a minutes-to-seconds conversion.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Not converting minutes to seconds, or confusing R with r

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Standard derivation of the cyclotron period that students often memorise.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming a faster particle takes less time to complete the circle

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires finding acceleration from $eE/m$ then applying uniform-acceleration kinematics.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using force instead of acceleration in the kinematics equation

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Simple $P \propto I^2$ scaling once the r.m.s. idea is understood.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking power scales linearly with current, or applying the sinusoidal factor $\sqrt{2}$

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: One-step use of $\lambda = h/(mv)$ comparing masses.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Associating the lightest particle with the smallest velocity

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Combines photon momentum with rate of change of momentum, including the factor of 2 on reflection.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Forgetting the factor of 2 for reflection, or using $p = h\lambda$

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Tests several subtle points: binding energy vs per nucleon, mass-energy in reactions, momentum conservation and decay independence.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Judging nuclear stability by total binding energy rather than binding energy per nucleon

mi-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs total binding energies (BE per nucleon × A) and their difference, not a difference of per-nucleon values.
mi-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Subtracting binding energies per nucleon instead of total binding energies

njc-2021-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must recall standard SI prefix powers.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The distinction follows directly from the meanings of precision and accuracy.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The diagram requires translating one vector and reversing the other.
