njc-2021-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must find the relative acceleration before applying a constant-acceleration equation.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Adding accelerations in the same direction

njc-2021-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must read three areas above the velocity of Y and solve for the plateau duration.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The vertical fall gives the flight time, which must then be used for the horizontal motion.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Using launch height as the fall distance

njc-2021-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must isolate the first triangular area, convert milliseconds and use the impulse to find the final velocity.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Using the full impulse through 200 ms

njc-2021-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish vector momentum from scalar kinetic energy and apply the elastic-collision condition.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming opposite velocities cancel kinetic energy

njc-2021-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The recoil speed follows from momentum conservation and must be squared in the kinetic-energy comparison.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Squaring the speed ratio without including the mass ratio

njc-2021-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The main steps are converting the mass and rate to SI units and applying Newton's second law in momentum form.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Using a per-minute rate as a per-second rate

njc-2021-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must interpret different angle references and choose an equilibrium component equation.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The problem combines moments, horizontal force balance and the distinction between the wall's force and the force on the wall.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Answering with the force on the shelf

njc-2021-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the origin of upthrust from the condition for floating equilibrium.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing displaced mass with displaced weight

njc-2021-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the initial slope and compare initial and final mechanical energy while accounting for drag.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Treating mechanical energy as conserved in a viscous fluid

njc-2021-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must turn volume flow into mass flow, then apply the head and efficiency to obtain useful power.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Reporting input power as output power

njc-2021-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must resolve weight along the slope, balance the forces and multiply by speed.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Using the full weight along the slope

njc-2021-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The calculation uses the period to find angular speed before applying the centripetal acceleration formula.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must identify the limiting normal force before calculating the speed.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q18.misconception: The track must exert a positive normal force at the minimum speed

njc-2021-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must find the bottom speed from energy conservation and then resolve the radial forces.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q19.misconception: The normal reaction equals the net centripetal force

njc-2021-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student reads an acceleration–displacement pair and converts the inferred angular frequency to a period.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q20.misconception: Angular frequency and period have the same numerical value

njc-2021-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must choose the sine form for an equilibrium crossing and evaluate it at one eighth of a cycle.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q21.misconception: Displacement is proportional to elapsed time in SHM

njc-2021-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must read velocity from the slope and acceleration from the displacement sign.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q22.misconception: Velocity has the sign of displacement

njc-2021-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish light damping from critical damping.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must turn a spatial snapshot of a moving wave into a time trace at a fixed point.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q24.misconception: The spatial slope gives the time slope directly

njc-2021-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must convert an intensity ratio to an amplitude ratio and identify the matching trace.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Intensity is directly proportional to displacement amplitude

njc-2021-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must keep intensity fixed while applying inverse-square spreading.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q26.misconception: Halving the power requires halving the distance

njc-2021-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student applies Malus’ law directly at the given angle.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Intensity follows the unsquared cosine projection

njc-2021-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must infer antiphase from the graphs and track the sign of the resultant.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q28.misconception: Partial cancellation leaves the resultant in phase with the smaller wave

njc-2021-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student counts the standing-wave loops and scales the frequency to the requested harmonic.

njc-2021-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must check both the node and antinode counts and the reversal of motion across each node.
njc-2021-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Neighbouring standing-wave regions move in phase

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student needs plausible estimates of sprint speed and body mass before applying the kinetic energy formula.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Kinetic energy scales linearly with speed

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Convert the percentage to an absolute uncertainty, then round to the corresponding place.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Reporting more digits than the uncertainty supports

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The ratio can be found by comparing areas on a speed–time graph or by splitting the motion into two intervals.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using the total distance for the second interval

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Resolve the launch velocity, update the vertical component, and recombine the components.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Applying gravity in the wrong direction

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Find the common velocity from momentum conservation before calculating the kinetic energy difference.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Confusing final kinetic energy with kinetic energy lost

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Identify the height difference between the mercury surfaces and use it to find the absolute pressure ratio.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing gauge pressure with absolute pressure

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Infer the line of action of the hinge force by extending the other two force lines and then determine its sense.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming the hinge force acts along the bonnet

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The answer follows directly from the definition of mechanical power.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing power with energy or momentum

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Convert the period to angular speed and substitute into the centripetal force equation.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using the period without squaring it

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Set up the inverse-square balance with two different distances and solve for the unknown position.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Treating gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Use inverse-distance scaling, subtract the initial potential, and multiply by mass.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing gravitational potential with gravitational potential energy

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The intended distinction is between microscopic energy exchange and net transfer at equilibrium.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing microscopic energy exchange with net heat transfer

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Read both states on the pressure–volume graph and combine the internal energy and work signs.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing work done on the gas with work done by it

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Distinguish heating from work and recognize how microscopic potential energy contributes to internal energy.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Translate the changing force into the sign and magnitude of the potential-energy gradient.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Confusing force with the potential-energy gradient

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Calculate the wavelength and express the separation as a fraction of a cycle.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using the separation alone as the fraction of a cycle

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Combines right-triangle geometry with the initial phase difference.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires the two fundamental air-column patterns and their frequency ratio.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires combining three field directions at one point.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Drawing fields away from negative charges

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires inferring the plate polarity and tracking two energy changes.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing terminal potential difference under load from e.m.f.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires tracing each probe point to its supply terminal with the filament open.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming intact lamps still divide the voltage

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires inferring both the torque and the horizontal resultant from the field lines.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal pole forces in a non-uniform field

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires using the change in enclosed area and converting both area and time.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming a uniform field guarantees constant flux

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires reading both oscilloscope scales and converting period to angular frequency.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires linking the cutoff to the maximum photon energy and inverting the voltage ratio.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming cutoff wavelength is proportional to voltage

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the slit width as the transverse position uncertainty before substituting.

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires connecting the undeflected majority to the relative size of the nucleus.
njc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing the evidence from undeflected and strongly deflected particles

njc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires comparing the penetration of the three radiations with the aluminium thickness.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Requires reversing one vector and recognising the resultant’s direction.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q1.misconception: Adding the original vector instead of its negative

njc-2022-promo-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing systematic shift from random scatter and understanding the role of averaging.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q3.difficultyReason: This requires applying one percentage-uncertainty rule and testing the listed values.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q3.misconception: Counting the uncertainty of a squared quantity only once.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must compare the bearings’ speeds after accounting for the delay between releases.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q4.misconception: Assuming equal accelerations imply equal velocities.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must connect the shapes of three graphs to the motion and changing forces.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing a declining height with a declining resultant force.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must model the ball and floor separately and equate their positions at contact.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q6.misconception: Treating the accelerating elevator floor as stationary after release.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must subtract opposing forces and combine the perpendicular components.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q7.misconception: Adding perpendicular force components as scalars.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The calculation requires converting grams to kilograms and assigning opposite signs to the two velocities.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q8.misconception: Subtracting speeds when the ball reverses direction.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must first use momentum conservation to find the lighter trolley’s speed, then add both kinetic energies.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q9.misconception: Assuming equal and opposite momenta also mean equal kinetic energies.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must infer the line of action of a contact force using both torque and force balance.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q10.misconception: Treating the resultant contact force as the normal force alone.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must find two different perpendicular lever arms before taking moments about the pin.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q11.misconception: Measuring the lever arm to the point of application instead of to the line of action.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must connect displaced air volume to upthrust and the force measured by the balance.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q12.misconception: Equating the balance reading with true weight in air.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the distance along the slope from the vertical rise and account for both energy transfers.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q13.misconception: Treating all the applied work as work against friction.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must combine two proportional relationships and recognise the resulting graph shape.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming power follows the same speed dependence as the resistive force.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must read two points and calculate the area over the added extension only.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q15.misconception: Using the final stored energy as the increase.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must resolve tension, eliminate it and express angular speed in terms of period.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q16.misconception: Using the bob’s weight as the magnitude of the tension.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must identify which force components are vertical and horizontal when the angle is measured from the ground.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q17.misconception: Reporting the angle to the vertical instead of to the horizontal.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q18.difficultyReason: It combines energy conservation over a two-radius rise with a radial force balance at the top.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q18.misconception: Using the bottom speed at the top

njc-2022-promo-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The three energy graphs can be distinguished by their shapes and values at the turning points.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish a squared sinusoid in time from the displacement relationships.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q21.difficultyReason: It requires tracking signed forces and extrapolating the upthrust graph to distinguish two similar options.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q21.misconception: Forgetting that upthrust vanishes at zero immersion

njc-2022-promo-p1-q22.difficultyReason: A small rightward shift of the profile reveals the instantaneous motion at both points.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q22.misconception: Reading the slope as the direction of particle motion

njc-2022-promo-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must read two ratios from the graph and square both.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q23.misconception: Ignoring one of the two squared factors

njc-2022-promo-p1-q24.difficultyReason: It is a direct substitution into Malus’ law.

njc-2022-promo-p1-q25.difficultyReason: It requires comparing three wavelength-to-diameter ratios and interpreting their order.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q25.misconception: Equating a larger minimum angle with better resolution

njc-2022-promo-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must compare the angle between the stars with a threshold that changes with wavelength.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q26.misconception: Assuming any decrease in wavelength guarantees resolution

njc-2022-promo-p1-q27.difficultyReason: It requires tracking three simultaneous changes in the double-slit formula.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q27.misconception: Treating slit separation as directly proportional to fringe spacing

njc-2022-promo-p1-q28.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing the common orbit from a property that depends on satellite mass.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming equal orbital speed implies equal kinetic energy

njc-2022-promo-p1-q29.difficultyReason: It requires converting altitude to distance from Earth’s centre before applying the inverse-square law.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q29.misconception: Using altitude in place of distance from Earth’s centre

njc-2022-promo-p1-q30.difficultyReason: It requires using the full separation in the gravitational force and half the separation in the centripetal term.
njc-2022-promo-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing the orbital radius with the separation between the stars

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: It requires recalling the definition of pressure and distinguishing quantities from named units.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing a physical quantity with its unit

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: It requires comparing the dimensions of square-root expressions with the dimensions of speed.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Overlooking how the square root acts on the units

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish decreasing acceleration from increasing speed during the fall.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Confusing terminal speed with terminal acceleration

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must find the common acceleration and then apply Newton’s second law to the passenger alone.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Confusing the normal force with the net force

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Choosing the centre of gravity as pivot reduces the problem to one moment equation.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using distances measured from the end of the beam

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must link constant acceleration to increasing speed and then to power.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming constant force supplies constant power

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must identify which speed is shared before applying the radius relation.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Equating angular speeds at a no-slip contact

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must compare spatial periods after both speed and frequency double.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming doubled frequency always halves wavelength

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must obtain the amplitude and locate the cloth relative to equilibrium before calculating speed.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Measuring SHM displacement from the highest point

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must interpret the energy graph and connect the maximum speed to the period.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing maximum speed with average speed

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must estimate the resolving angle and convert it to a separation at the given distance.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing angular resolution with linear separation

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student must read the local spacing and use the sign of the potential gradient.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Taking the field direction to be toward higher potential

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must account for Earth’s rotation and distinguish the normal force from the gravitational force.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Assuming a larger centripetal acceleration raises apparent weight

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must express the fixed resistor’s power in terms of the total series resistance.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Treating the variable resistance as the resistor whose power is plotted

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must relate the lower parallel load resistance to the battery’s terminal voltage.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming the battery supplies a fixed total current

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must apply the null condition to both potentiometer branches simultaneously.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Assuming balanced potentiometer branches still load the wire

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must translate equipotential spacing into a graph of electric field strength.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing electric potential with electric field strength

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Students must compare the vector sums and distinguish field, potential, energy and force.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Treating electric field as a scalar.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Students must the definition of thermal equilibrium gives the result directly.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing absorption rate with equilibrium temperature.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Students must square the speed ratio before relating it to the volume at constant pressure.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming volume scales linearly with r.m.s. speed.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Students must use the common pressure and account for both volumes and temperatures.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Students must identify how two steady runs can eliminate the heat-loss term.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Changing the temperatures while assuming heat loss stays constant.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Students must apply the first law to compression with negligible heat transfer.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Equating a temperature rise with heat supplied.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Students must read the angle to the field and account for the halved flux density.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Using the rotation angle as the angle to the field.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Students must track the field strength with distance and apply a directional rule for polarity.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming constant speed gives constant motional e.m.f.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Students must extract the peak current from a graph of its square and then compute the r.m.s. value.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Reading the peak of an $I^2$ graph as current.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish what controls photoelectron energy from what controls the emission rate.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Assuming brighter light increases each photon’s energy.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students must link momentum to wavelength and then to the size of the diffraction rings.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Assuming faster electrons spread through larger angles.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Students must subtract the rest energies and decide whether energy is absorbed or released.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing energy required for breakup with energy released.

njc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Students must track the two half-life counts separately and then add the remaining activities.
njc-2023-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Averaging the activities instead of adding them.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: A single rate estimate and time conversion are sufficient.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing a per-minute rate with an hourly count.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must recognising a zero error as a fixed offset identifies the technique directly.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Expecting repeated measurements to remove a fixed offset.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student combines a constant-acceleration equation with the kinetic energy formula.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming kinetic energy has the same displacement dependence as speed.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must count the elapsed intervals and subtract two free-fall distances.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Counting drops instead of elapsed intervals.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student finds the common acceleration and then identifies which friction force the question asks for.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Confusing friction on A with friction on B.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student compares moments using the perpendicular component of each force.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using the full force when it is oblique.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student distinguishes the conservation rules for elastic and inelastic collisions.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming total kinetic energy is always conserved.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student must combine energy and momentum conservation and recognise that both masses share a speed at maximum compression.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming all initial kinetic energy becomes elastic energy.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must recognise that the normal force vanishes at detachment and resolve the weight radially.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the full gravitational acceleration as the radial component.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student recalls the equatorial orbit and Earth-matched period and recognises that satellite mass is irrelevant.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming satellite mass determines orbital period.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student recalls the definition of a uniform field and distinguishes strength from potential.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Confusing a constant field with constant potential.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student computes the arithmetic mean and the root mean square from the same three speeds.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Taking the arithmetic mean instead of the root mean square.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must hold the valve pressure and cylinder volume fixed and convert both temperatures to kelvin.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures in an ideal gas ratio.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student locates the equilibrium and finds the separate travel times on either side of it.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Treating a displacement interval as a single displacement from equilibrium.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student converts distances from equilibrium into possible phases before comparing the particles.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Taking a phase from equilibrium instead of the difference between the two phases.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must square both ratios and combine the effects of the two changes.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using unsquared ratios or reversing the amplitude change.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student must calculate the two diffraction angles separately and take their difference.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Subtracting diffraction orders before taking the inverse sine.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Reads both potentials and slopes and tracks the charge sign.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing electric potential and potential energy

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Combines the uniform field formula with Newton’s second law.

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires recognising equipotential junctions in the rearranged circuit.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Mistaking an equipotential link for a short across a lamp

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires calculating energy per unit charge for each resistor and for the battery.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Swapping internal and external voltage drops

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the force pair and using the full perpendicular separation to find its torque.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Using half the separation as the couple arm

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Combines the energy gained during acceleration with the speed selected by crossed fields.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Failing to square the selected speed

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires finding the squared-radius dependence and subtracting the two centre-to-point e.m.f.s.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Assuming e.m.f. scales linearly with radius

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Uses the graph slope for the magnitude and Lenz’s law for the direction.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Confusing flux linkage with its rate of change

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires following both diode paths and comparing the resulting current peaks.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Treating the resistor current as half-wave rectified

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Links photocurrent to intensity and takes the square root of the ratio.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Treating amplitude as proportional to intensity

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires estimating the energy of a red photon and comparing it with level differences.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Using a level energy instead of the energy gap

njc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires tracking the separate nucleon and proton number changes.
njc-2024-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Ignoring the proton-number increase in beta-minus decay

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Uses a familiar mass estimate and scales it to twelve coins.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Estimating the mass of one coin instead of twelve

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires expressing density in terms of the measurements and doubling the diameter contribution.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Counting the diameter uncertainty only once

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires one substitution in the constant-acceleration displacement equation.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using maximum height as the displacement at the specified time

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Resolve the pull, subtract friction and apply Newton’s second law.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student needs signed momenta, a common velocity and the final kinetic energy.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must combine perpendicular tension components and use the force ratio to scale the extension.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: The student must relate the disc torque to the couple on the lever.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Omitting one force of the couple

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student combines volume flow, gravitational energy loss and efficiency.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Confusing input power with useful output

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student equates limiting friction to the centripetal force and solves for angular speed in SI units.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Confusing angular speed with its square or with linear speed

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student only needs to distinguish gravitational field strength from spacecraft acceleration.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing gravitational force with apparent weight

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student divides the two field equations and takes a square root.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming radius is proportional to mass at fixed surface gravity

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student links cooling to melting and adds the original water mass.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing melted mass with total water mass

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation is a single signed addition.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Treating work done by the system as an energy gain

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the dependence on height from the dependence on spring extension.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Treating displacement from equilibrium as spring extension

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student compares amplitudes across the frequency range and checks the direction of the peak shift.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Assuming damping increases amplitude away from resonance

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish field amplitude from intensity and interpret the angle to the filter axis.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Applying the intensity factor to the field amplitude

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: The student must identify which pair makes both changes increase spreading.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Judging diffraction from gap width or wavelength alone

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student converts line density to spacing, calculates two diffraction angles and finds their difference.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Assuming equal angular spacing between orders

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The force follows directly from squaring the separation ratio.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Treating an inverse-square law as inverse-linear

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must identify the energy conversion and use both nuclear charges in the potential energy.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Treating an alpha particle as singly charged

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The formula is direct, but the square-millimetre conversion must be handled correctly.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Students must identify the active wire segment, find the voltage division and square the voltage ratio.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming power scales linearly with voltage

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The perpendicular-wire force law must be applied to the changes, with the length in metres.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish how mass affects the radius and acceleration when the magnetic force is fixed.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming equal force implies equal acceleration

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The given expression requires computing angular speed and maximum flux linkage before substitution.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must read the peak of the squared-current graph and convert mean square to current.

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Students must convert picometres, calculate momentum from wavelength and convert momentum to kinetic energy.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Dropping the factor of two in the kinetic energy formula

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must combine three decay changes and work backwards from X on the graph.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Applying beta-minus decay with the wrong sign

njc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must convert the parent-to-daughter ratio to the surviving fraction and compare it with successive half-lives.
njc-2025-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Confusing a parent-to-daughter ratio with the surviving fraction

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Rearranging the fractional-uncertainty sum with the power of 2 on t.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting to double the percentage uncertainty in t, or adding instead of subtracting

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Single order-of-magnitude estimate from everyday knowledge.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Poor sense of scale when converting cm to m³

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: One resolution of weight along the slope set equal to the given maximum friction.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using cosine instead of sine for the component along the slope

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires the perpendicular distance from O to side BA in a regular hexagon.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Taking the distance OB instead of the perpendicular distance to the line of action

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Best solved by noticing both masses share the same acceleration, so relative motion is uniform.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Thinking the accelerations make the relative motion non-uniform

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Needs recognising that equal time intervals require heights in the ratio 1:4:9:16.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming equally spaced beads give equally spaced sounds

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Efficiency then P = Fv with constant velocity.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Using input power instead of useful output power

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Qualitative use of $F = mr\omega^2$ with friction providing the centripetal force.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Thinking objects further out have a larger angular velocity

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Resolving tension for a conical pendulum and converting angular velocity to period.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the wrong trigonometric ratio when resolving tension

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Ratio of orbital speeds; main trap is measuring distance from the surface instead of the centre.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Using distance from Earth's surface instead of from its centre

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Using an inverse-square dependence on radius for potential

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Reading the gradient of an a–x graph and taking a square root.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Forgetting to square-root the gradient to get ω

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs particle direction from the wave's travel direction plus phase difference from the separation in wavelengths.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Getting the direction of particle motion wrong for a travelling wave

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Uses width ratio for distance, then inverse-square intensity and amplitude ∝ √I.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Thinking amplitude falls in the same proportion as intensity

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Compare fundamental frequencies of closed and open pipes, then check harmonics.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Treating open and closed pipes as having the same fundamental for the same length

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires using the longest wavelength to limit complete orders and counting both sides.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Using the shortest wavelength, or forgetting orders on both sides

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Needs conservation of total moles with equal final pressures and kelvin temperatures.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures or assuming moles stay proportional to volume

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Eliminating the unknown heat loss with two simultaneous equations.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Ignoring heat loss to the surroundings

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Summing scalar potentials and multiplying by a negative charge with care over signs.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Sign error from forgetting the electron's negative charge

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Option D needs a vector sum of fields at Z before and after; the difference is small.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming field strength at Z must decrease because one charge moves

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Turns ratio then Ohm's law and power with r.m.s. values.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Using the peak-power doubling or inverting the turns ratio

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: One substitution of Q = It into C = Q/V with prefix handling.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Prefix or power-of-ten slip with micro/milli

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Recognise two groups of three parallel capacitors joined in series.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing series and parallel combination rules for capacitors

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Must realise the velocity selector fixes equal speeds, then use r = mv/(qB) as a ratio.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming the ions have equal kinetic energy or forgetting both mass and charge change

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Combines F = BIL to find BL, SHM maximum speed, and motional e.m.f. BLv.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Using amplitude or frequency directly as the speed instead of v0 = ωx0

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Needs E0 = NBAω so doubling frequency doubles both peak e.m.f. and frequency.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Thinking only the frequency changes and the peak e.m.f. stays the same

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Standard photoelectric fact: intensity affects photon rate only.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Believing light intensity changes the threshold frequency or electron energy

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Convert both wavelengths to photon energies and compare against two work functions in an unfamiliar electroscope setup.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Thinking shorter wavelength light always causes emission regardless of work function

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires knowing that the closer alpha particle feels greater repulsion and is deflected more.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Thinking alpha particles are attracted to the nucleus or that farther particles deflect more

njc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Must read P's half-life directly and find D1's half-life from its tail after P has decayed.
njc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Reading D1's half-life from its peak or from the start rather than its exponential tail

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Identifying the variable reaction delay distinguishes the one random error from three consistent biases.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q1.misconception: Confusing random variation with consistent bias

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Students must distinguish the free-fall gradients from the steeper gradient during contact.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q2.misconception: Assuming acceleration reverses when velocity reverses

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Students must resolve the launch velocity, update the vertical component and recombine the components.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q3.misconception: Adding perpendicular velocity components as scalars

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must find the acceleration of the whole system and then resolve the tension on the bob.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q4.misconception: Ignoring friction or measuring the angle from the horizontal

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must identify which body each force acts on.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q5.misconception: Treating two forces on one body as an action–reaction pair

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student must convert each pressure to a force and distinguish upthrust from the net force.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q6.misconception: Including the block’s weight in the buoyant force

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The student calculates useful power and then divides by efficiency to find the input power.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q8.misconception: Multiplying the useful output power by efficiency

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The student must compare how mass, radius and maximum friction affect the slipping threshold.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q9.misconception: Comparing maximum friction without comparing the required force

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The student must connect gravitational field strength to the changing slope of a velocity–time graph.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing the sign of velocity with the sign of acceleration

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q11.difficultyReason: The student must relate total orbital energy to gravitational potential energy before taking the difference.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q11.misconception: Equating the increase in potential energy with the increase in total energy

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The student distinguishes latent heat per unit mass from the energy changes during melting.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q12.misconception: Confusing latent heat per kilogram with total absorbed energy

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The student must rearrange the mean kinetic energy equation and square the speed ratio.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q13.misconception: Using r.m.s. speed in place of its square

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The student applies the first law twice and relates the changes in internal energy to the temperature changes.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q14.misconception: Using a positive sign for work done by the gas

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student identifies the displacement from equilibrium and converts period to angular frequency.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q15.misconception: Measuring amplitude from the spring’s natural length

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student recalls the ordering of the three named damping regimes.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q16.misconception: Treating critical damping as the strongest damping

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The student interprets the dry spots as antinodes and uses their spacing to calculate frequency.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q18.misconception: Using adjacent antinode spacing as the full wavelength

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student finds the first-minimum angle and doubles it for the full central width.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q19.misconception: Using the angle to one first minimum as the full width

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The student must identify the quantities that determine energy when the time is unknown.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must link the voltage divider to the balance length.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q21.misconception: Increasing the voltage across PQ lengthens the balance length.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: The student must infer the initial force balance and determine how it changes.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming a new equilibrium in a uniform field.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must determine four field directions and resolve and combine their components.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q23.misconception: Adding magnetic flux densities as scalars.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must combine magnetic and centripetal force and identify what determines the period.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q24.misconception: Assuming a longer orbit always takes longer.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must project both wire segments and apply Fleming’s left-hand rule.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q25.misconception: Using the angle to the normal as the angle to the field.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must read the slope on the falling segment and multiply by the coil area and turns.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q26.misconception: Using the average field change from the start of the graph.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The question directly tests the heating interpretation of r.m.s. current.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing the mean current with its heating equivalent.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must account for both the transformer turns ratio and half-wave rectification before finding the r.m.s. current.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q28.misconception: Applying the unrectified secondary voltage directly across the load.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish photon energy, photon arrival rate and photoelectron speed.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q29.misconception: Confusing light intensity with energy per photon.

nyjc-2021-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must filter transitions by the visible range before comparing their wavelengths.
nyjc-2021-other-p1-q30.misconception: Choosing the smallest energy gap without checking visibility.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The student must judge orders of magnitude across several physical contexts.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Overestimating the upper limit of human hearing.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must rearrange the formula and express kinetic energy in base units.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Leaving derived units in an SI base-unit answer.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must rearrange for mass and compare four fractional uncertainties weighted by their powers.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Comparing fractional uncertainties without weighting by the exponents.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: The student must construct a velocity triangle with an eastward wind and a due-north resultant.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Treating the still-air speed as the northward component.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must read signed areas and divide the displacement by total time.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Using total distance to calculate average velocity.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: It requires tracking drag separately in the horizontal and vertical directions.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Treating a projectile with drag like a projectile in vacuum.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: It requires finding the moving fragment’s momentum and using it to calculate kinetic energy.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Assuming kinetic energy is conserved in an explosion.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: It requires locating the intersection of two lines of action and tracing the contact force through it.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Treating the normal reaction as the entire contact force.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: It requires comparing the force components and moments independently in four diagrams.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming nonzero torque implies a nonzero resultant force.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: It requires using the displacement direction to determine work and accounting for the gain in height.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Equating constant kinetic energy with zero work by each force.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: It requires recognizing that each block moves half the initial separation and using both masses in the energy balance.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Using the full initial separation as each block’s displacement.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: It requires applying the definition of a radian to a labelled arc and radius.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Inverting the arc length and radius.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: It requires estimating a tangent gradient from the secant that best brackets the target point.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Using potential divided by distance instead of the local potential gradient.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing signed potential change from work, kinetic energy gain and field-strength change.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing a change in potential with the magnitude of the fall in potential.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: It requires reading a half-cycle phase slip from the graphs and using it to find a full-cycle slip.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Mistaking antiphase for the next occurrence of equal phase.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: It requires connecting constant melting temperature to one component of internal energy.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Assuming energy absorbed during melting raises temperature.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: It requires finding the wavelength and expressing the separation as a fraction of one cycle.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Using a phase change of half a turn for a whole wavelength.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: It requires dividing by the wavefront area and converting the detector area before multiplying.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Using the numerical value in square centimetres as square metres.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: It requires distinguishing the frequency, phase and amplitude of points on adjacent loops.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Assuming points with the same amplitude are in phase.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: It requires tracking energy and the charge sign, then distinguishing an average field component from a uniform field.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Inferring a uniform electric field from an endpoint potential difference.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires reading a parallel circuit and interpreting potential difference as energy per unit charge.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Adding the potential differences of parallel branches

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires using the ammeter null to link two potential-divider calculations.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Assuming zero ammeter current means zero current in both loops

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires linking the energy gain to magnetic circular motion and eliminating speed.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Failing to square the radius when eliminating speed

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires differentiating flux linkage and connecting the maximum slope to the coil orientation.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Equating maximum flux linkage with maximum induced e.m.f.

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires reading the durations of a nonsinusoidal waveform and taking a time-weighted root mean square.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Averaging current magnitudes instead of squared currents

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Requires calculating current on the load side at two resistances and converting to mains current.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Confusing secondary current with mains current

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the cutoff wavelength, characteristic peaks and overall intensity.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Using intensity or peak count to infer accelerating voltage

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Requires combining the activity and half-life equations to rank four samples by a ratio.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Comparing half-life or amount of substance on its own

nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Requires comparing each absorber count with the unshielded count and the background level.
nyjc-2022-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Taking every count above zero as evidence of source radiation

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the spread and centre of a measurement distribution.

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing variable timing error from a consistent measurement bias.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q2.misconception: Treating background count fluctuations and omission of the background correction as the same error

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Requires reasoning about vertical motion independently of horizontal motion.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q3.misconception: Using total launch speed to determine the time of flight

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Requires isolating the trailer and using its share of the total resistance.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q4.misconception: Treating tow-bar tension as the net force on the trailer

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Requires finding the off-centre weight deficit and balancing its moment against the applied force and friction couple.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q5.misconception: Using the cylinder radius as the couple arm

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Requires checking the lines of action for the whole structure and the hinge forces on the individual rods.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q6.misconception: Ignoring friction in the floor reaction or treating hinge forces as independent

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q8.difficultyReason: The calculation requires finding the drop of the water’s centre of mass before applying efficiency.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q8.misconception: Using the surface height for all the water

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q9.difficultyReason: The diagram requires identifying the inward resultant of the tilted lift and weight.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q9.misconception: Treating centripetal force as a separate force

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q10.difficultyReason: The main step is recognizing that constant linear speed makes angular speed inversely proportional to radius.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q10.misconception: Confusing constant linear speed with constant angular speed

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The first law applies once the student identifies the net heat transfer and the energy change of the contents.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing heat entering with net heat supplied

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The calculation is a signed sum once the two microscopic energy terms are identified.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q14.misconception: Including bulk mechanical energy in internal energy

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The graphs can be distinguished using the initial kinetic energy and its period.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q15.misconception: Giving kinetic energy the same period as displacement

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The student must connect the phase difference to the resultant amplitude and then square the amplitude to obtain intensity.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q16.misconception: Adding intensities directly for coherent waves

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Identifying the nodes and antinode gives the required phase relationships directly.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q17.misconception: Confusing the component waves with the standing-wave profiles

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The calculation uses the core diameter for the turn length and the wire diameter for the cross-sectional area.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q18.misconception: Swapping the coil and wire diameters

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student must infer equal midpoint potentials and relate the voltage drops to resistance ratios.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q19.misconception: Equating resistance differences in a balanced bridge

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The two balance lengths must be converted to voltages and used with the loaded-cell current.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q20.misconception: Equating the open-circuit e.m.f. with the loaded terminal voltage

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must write two signed force equations and eliminate the weight before using the field strength.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q21.misconception: Treating the change in net force as the electric force

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Ranking the fields requires identifying cancelling pairs and comparing the remaining vector sums.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q22.misconception: Adding field magnitudes without accounting for direction

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: The student must balance the forces and check which magnetic-field direction produces the required opposing force.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q23.misconception: Choosing fields without checking the directions of the forces

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must infer the induced current along a moving radius and trace its return path through the resistor.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q24.misconception: Applying the flux through the whole disc to the moving radius

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Find the lamp current, add the parallel currents, then apply ideal transformer power balance.

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Use the photon energy to rule out copper, then compare the stopping voltages.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q27.misconception: Reading stopping voltage from the saturation current

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Distinguish the characteristic peaks from the continuous spectrum and its cutoff.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q28.misconception: Confusing characteristic peaks with the short-wavelength cutoff

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Convert MeV to joules and use mass–energy equivalence with the correct sign.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q29.misconception: Forgetting the mega prefix or reversing the mass change

nyjc-2023-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Use changes in binding energy per nucleon to identify the false statement.
nyjc-2023-other-p1-q30.misconception: Assuming fission releases energy for light nuclei

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Expand work and charge into SI base units to find the units of voltage.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q1.misconception: Dropping mass when expanding the unit of force

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Calculate the reaction and braking distances separately before adding them.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q2.misconception: Omitting the distance travelled during the reaction time

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Combine two displacement equations with the just-reaches condition to eliminate the unknown speed and acceleration.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q3.misconception: Assuming equal initial speeds imply equal distances

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Recall Newton’s second law in momentum form.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q4.misconception: Identifying one force as the resultant during impact

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Read the lift’s free-body diagram and connect a zero resultant to zero acceleration.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q5.misconception: Equating zero acceleration with being at rest

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Find both perpendicular lever arms about the step edge and balance moments at the tipping threshold.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q6.misconception: Measuring lever arms from the drum centre

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Include the gravitational energy lost during compression and use the spring’s increasing force to obtain its maximum.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q7.misconception: Using the average spring force as the maximum

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Calculate the required inward force and compare it with the friction limit.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q8.misconception: Treating centrifugal force as a real braking force

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Use conservation of energy to determine the speed term, then apply the radial force equation.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q9.misconception: Equating tension to the net centripetal force

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Use the two distances from Earth’s centre and express the change in potential energy in terms of surface weight.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q10.misconception: Assuming weight stays constant over a height of two Earth radii

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Relates the volume and density ratios and converts both temperatures to kelvin.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q11.misconception: Using Celsius temperatures in gas-law ratios

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Requires weighting the two temperature changes by the blocks’ different heat capacities.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q12.misconception: Averaging temperatures without weighting by heat capacity

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Requires inferring the motion period from the energy graph and using peak energy to find acceleration.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q13.misconception: Confusing the kinetic-energy period with the SHM period

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that a projection of uniform circular motion has a varying speed.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q14.misconception: Assuming the shadow inherits the bob’s constant speed

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the conditions for fringe contrast from the condition for stability.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q16.misconception: Equating coherence with zero phase difference

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Requires translating both asymmetric pulses and adding signed displacements over the overlap.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q17.misconception: Adding pulse magnitudes instead of signed displacements

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Requires selecting the two distances to the target point and adding signed scalar contributions.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q18.misconception: Using the separation between charges in the potential calculation

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing the value of a potential from its spatial gradient.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing zero potential with zero potential gradient

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that opposite charges moving in opposite directions produce currents in the same direction.

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires tracing the lamp terminals in four variable-resistor configurations.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q21.misconception: Assuming a parallel resistor can vary the load voltage of an ideal supply

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Requires identifying the two relevant resistors within one branch of a parallel network.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q22.misconception: Including a parallel branch in a series potential-divider ratio

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q23.difficultyReason: Requires combining the right-hand grip rule with Fleming’s left-hand rule at two points.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q23.misconception: Applying parallel-wire attraction rules to perpendicular wires

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Requires identifying which coil dimension controls how fast the area inside the field changes.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q24.misconception: Confusing total flux change with its rate of change

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Requires reading peak power and separating the power period from the current period.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q25.misconception: Taking the power period as the source period

nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Requires tracking which half-cycle a series or shunt diode passes to the load.
nyjc-2024-a-level-p1-q26.misconception: Ignoring the polarity of the half-cycle passed by the diode

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q12.difficultyReason: The two temperatures can be compared directly using one kinetic-theory relation.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q12.misconception: Mean kinetic energy scales with particle mass or pressure.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q13.difficultyReason: The calculation requires substituting mass density and converting kilopascals to pascals.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q13.misconception: Using the wrong pressure units or kinetic-theory factor.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q14.difficultyReason: The cycle requires interpreting pressure–volume areas, temperature and heat transfer.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing heat transfer with work or internal-energy change.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q15.difficultyReason: The student must infer wave travel from the motion at Q and check both possible positions of P.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q15.misconception: Confusing particle motion with wave propagation.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q16.difficultyReason: The graph gives the phase once the student accounts for the intervening complete cycle.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q16.misconception: Reading zero velocity at a turning point as zero acceleration.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q18.difficultyReason: The node and antinode boundary conditions determine which multiples of the fundamental are allowed.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q18.misconception: Allowing even harmonics in a pipe with one closed end.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q19.difficultyReason: The student converts hours to seconds, reads the graph area and uses it to calculate energy.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q19.misconception: Using the peak current for the whole interval.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q20.difficultyReason: The graph must be read at a specified current and interpreted using power and resistance relations.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q20.misconception: Treating the local graph slope as the reciprocal of resistance.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q21.difficultyReason: The student must reduce the parallel pair and use the resulting voltage division to find a power ratio.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q21.misconception: Assuming equal resistances dissipate equal power.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Solving the question requires identifying the null condition and how the driver circuit sets the wire's potential gradient.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q22.misconception: Assuming internal resistance changes terminal voltage even at zero current.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q23.difficultyReason: This follows directly from the relationship between field direction and potential gradient.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q23.misconception: Confusing potential with electric field magnitude.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q24.difficultyReason: The student must identify the magnetic couple and project the coil width to find the perpendicular separation.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q24.misconception: Using the coil angle to project the wrong lever arm.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q25.difficultyReason: The student must determine the field orientation and divide the flux-linkage change by time.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q25.misconception: Using change in flux linkage without dividing by time.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q26.difficultyReason: The student must average the squared voltage over the full period, including the zero half-cycle.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q26.misconception: Applying the unrectified sinusoidal RMS formula to a half-wave waveform.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q27.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the roles of stopping voltage and saturation current.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q27.misconception: Using saturation current to infer frequency.

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q28.difficultyReason: The student must link the accelerating potential to momentum, then convert the de Broglie wavelength to a photon frequency.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q28.misconception: Equating photon energy with electron kinetic energy

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q29.difficultyReason: The student must identify the endpoint and subtract the beta particle’s share of the energy.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q29.misconception: Using the spectrum peak as the decay energy

nyjc-2025-other-p1-q30.difficultyReason: The student must subtract the same unknown background from both readings before applying two half-lives.
nyjc-2025-other-p1-q30.misconception: Applying the half-life to the total measured rate

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: Single rearrangement of SI base units.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Forgetting that angular speed has unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ or misexpressing the joule

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: Compare fractional uncertainties with the power of D, and ignore the irrelevant R.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Comparing absolute instead of fractional uncertainties, or including irrelevant data

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: Must use extensions from natural length, not the change in length directly.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Using the 10 mm change in length as the extension

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Tests precise conditions for equilibrium and properties of a couple.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Believing zero resultant force alone guarantees equilibrium

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: Must deduce the sign convention (downward positive) from the graph before judging each statement.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Assuming upward is positive and so misreading which point is the maximum upward velocity

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: Must model mass flow rate ρAv and the rate of KE transfer, with area from diameter.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Using radius-diameter confusion or forgetting the ½ in kinetic energy

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.difficultyReason: Interpret area under a force–displacement graph as work done by each force.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q7.misconception: Confusing the gain in kinetic energy (P) with the energy dissipated

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.difficultyReason: Two-step ratio: fall time scales with the square root of height.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q8.misconception: Assuming horizontal distance is proportional to the drop height

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.difficultyReason: Uses Newton's third law to get the force on Y from X's momentum change.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q9.misconception: Using the speed change of Y without knowing its final velocity, or ignoring direction

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.difficultyReason: Must bound v using energy conservation: enough to rise above the centre but not enough to complete the loop.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q10.misconception: Thinking v = √(gr) at the bottom is the condition for completing the loop

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.difficultyReason: Direct use of Kepler's third law with a ratio.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q11.misconception: Assuming period is proportional to radius

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the defining features of a geostationary orbit.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q12.misconception: Thinking orbital radius depends on the satellite's mass

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.difficultyReason: Needs linking x = 0 at t = 0 to maximum KE and recognising KE never goes negative and has twice the frequency.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q13.misconception: Plotting KE with the same shape and frequency as displacement

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.difficultyReason: Requires reading displacements off a longitudinal-particle diagram and deducing particle velocity from wave direction.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q14.misconception: Confusing compression/rarefaction position with direction of particle motion

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.difficultyReason: Standard crest/trough reading of a two-source wavefront diagram.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q15.misconception: Thinking the gap between wavefronts (trough-trough) gives cancellation

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.difficultyReason: Needs computing angular separation and aperture from Rayleigh criterion, then checking each statement.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q16.misconception: Thinking a longer wavelength improves resolution

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the kinetic theory assumptions.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q17.misconception: Believing all gas molecules have the same speed

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.difficultyReason: Needs recognising zero net change in U over a cycle, finding enclosed area and its sign, then applying the first law.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q18.misconception: Getting the sign of work done on the gas wrong for a clockwise cycle

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.difficultyReason: Needs scalar superposition of potentials and the sign convention for work done by the field.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q19.misconception: Confusing work done by the field with work done by an external agent

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.difficultyReason: Single Coulomb's-law substitution, with care over the pico prefix and alpha charge.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q20.misconception: Using the electron charge for the alpha particle or mis-converting pm

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.difficultyReason: Requires recognising that current flows radially, so the depth sets the cross-sectional area, not the length.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q21.misconception: Taking the liquid depth as the conductor length

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.difficultyReason: Needs reasoning about where potential difference appears across a break in a series circuit.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q22.misconception: Thinking a voltmeter across a broken component reads zero

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q23.misconception: Mixing up the series and parallel rules for capacitors

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.difficultyReason: Needs fields from two wires and recognising the two contributions are perpendicular.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q24.misconception: Adding or subtracting the two fields as if parallel

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.difficultyReason: Needs applying Lenz's law to eddy currents in an unfamiliar set-up.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q25.misconception: Expecting no interaction because aluminium is non-magnetic

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.difficultyReason: Chains transformer power, peak-to-r.m.s. conversion and $I^2R$ loss.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q26.misconception: Using the peak voltage instead of the r.m.s. voltage

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.difficultyReason: Needs realising photon momentum and photon rate both depend on wavelength and cancel.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q27.misconception: Thinking pressure depends on photon momentum alone, not the photon rate

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.difficultyReason: Direct recall of the probabilistic interpretation of the wavefunction.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q28.misconception: Picturing the electron as following a definite orbit

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.difficultyReason: Needs normalising activity per gram before applying exponential decay.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q29.misconception: Comparing activities without scaling for sample mass

nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.difficultyReason: Needs energy release as the increase in total binding energy, counting nucleons correctly.
nyjc-2026-prelim-p1-q30.misconception: Including free neutrons in the product binding energy

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q1.difficultyReason: The question requires recognising the SI base units and distinguishing them from a quantity and a derived unit.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q1.misconception: Treating gram as the SI base unit for mass

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q2.difficultyReason: The student must assess several order-of-magnitude estimates, including an ideal-gas estimate with a plausible classroom volume.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q2.misconception: Underestimating the moles of air in a classroom

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q3.difficultyReason: The student must distinguish the slope of a displacement–time graph from a change in that slope.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q3.misconception: Reading acceleration directly from a displacement–time slope

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q4.difficultyReason: Finding the relevant velocity requires resolving and adding two velocities before solving the vertical displacement equation.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q4.misconception: Using only one contribution to the initial vertical velocity

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q5.difficultyReason: The student must take a signed area and convert the velocity change to a momentum change.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q5.misconception: Adding the area below the time axis

ri-2017-prelim-p1-q6.difficultyReason: The student needs to recognise a standard consequence of momentum and kinetic-energy conservation.
ri-2017-prelim-p1-q6.misconception: Assuming all elastic collisions exchange particle speeds
